Core Framework/Overview

Core Framework Overview

The Ultimate AAA Inspector & Tooling Architecture for Unity.
Built for Unity 6 (6000.x)+.

Welcome to MSUltimate

MSUltimate elevates the Unity Inspector from a plain serialization window into a responsive, beautiful, high-efficiency authoring environment. Designed for enterprise production pipelines, MSUltimate delivers zero-boilerplate attributes, dynamic layout groups, scene debug overlays, and deep editor tooling.

New to the ecosystem? Read the Ecosystem & Edition Comparison Guide for a comprehensive breakdown of Community, Pro, and Addon packages.

Modules in this Suite

  • MSUltimate Core — 156 concrete attributes (161 documented attribute classes including base contracts), custom collection serializers, extended types, and modular windowing framework.
  • Animated Attributes — 99 concrete reactive visual feedback, VFX, and kinetic motion attributes (101 attribute classes).
  • Component Designer — 74 concrete header cards, themes, and aesthetic styling attributes (75 attribute classes).
  • Hierarchy Designer — 82 concrete hierarchy enhancement and telemetry attributes (83 attribute classes).
  • ToolBox Vol. 1 — Advanced Console, History Track, Lifetime Track, and Live Track (+ 4 attributes).
  • Validation Module — 39 real-time validation attributes and project scan window.
  • Inspector Customizer — Non-destructive virtual attribute engine, Makeover Graph, AI Decorator, templates/recipes, and AST code baking.

Core Framework/Overview & Architecture/Core Systems Architecture

Core Systems Architecture

Technical overview of MSUltimate's drawer discovery database, UI Toolkit rendering pipeline, custom collection serializers, extended types, modular windowing, and global settings.

Systems Overview

  • Drawer Discovery & Reflection Caching: Domain-reload TypeCache discovery via DrawerDatabase pairing ModularAttribute types to BaseDrawer / ModularDrawer<T> implementations.
  • Drawer Stacking & Layout Pipeline: Execution order combining layout groups (BoxGroup, HorizontalGroup, BeginTabGroup, BeginSplitPane), conditionals (ShowIf, EnableIf, ConditionExpressionEngine), decorators, and value drawers in ModularMonoBehaviourEditor.
  • Custom Serializers & Extended Types: ISerializationCallbackReceiver collections (SerializableDictionary<TKey, TValue>, SerializableHashSet<T>, SerializableMatrix2D<T>, SerializableMatrix3D<T>, SerializableQueue<T>, SerializableStack<T>) and extended types (SerializableDateTime, SerializableNullable<T>, SerializableRange<T>, SerializableTuple<T1, T2>, SerializableTuple<T1, T2, T3>, SerializableType).
  • Modular Windowing System: [ModularWindow], [ShowInWindow], ModularEditorWindow, ModularMenuEditorWindow, ModularMenuTree, ModularModalWindow, and ModularAssetManagerWindow.
  • Preferences, Defaults & Setup: Global responsive label/layout defaults (MSUltimateLayoutSettings), global component defaults/ignore rules (MSUltimateComponentDefaultsSettings), and zero-inheritance type baking (MSUltimateSetupWizard / MSUltimateTypeBaker).

Core Framework/Overview & Architecture/MSUltimate Ecosystem & Edition Comparison Guide

MSUltimate Ecosystem & Edition Comparison Guide

Welcome to the MSUltimate Architecture.
Built natively for Unity 6 (6000.x)+ across Universal (URP), High Definition (HDRP), and Built-in (BiRP) Render Pipelines.

1. Overview & Ecosystem Vision

MSUltimate is a modular, enterprise-grade Unity Editor enhancement suite designed to transform the Unity Inspector, Scene Hierarchy, and development toolchain into a fast, beautiful, and deeply structured production environment.

Built from the ground up on Unity's modern UI Toolkit (with seamless IMGUI fallback), MSUltimate eliminates per-frame layout recalculations, delivers buttery-smooth 120 FPS+ inspector scrolling, and introduces zero garbage collection (GC) or build bloat to your standalone game builds.

To accommodate solo indie developers, specialized teams, and large studios alike, MSUltimate is distributed across three primary paths:

  1. MSUltimate Core (Community Edition): A generous, 100% free foundational inspector engine for qualifying indie creators.
  2. MSUltimate Core (Pro Edition): Full C# source code access to the core engine with no revenue restrictions.
  3. 6 Specialized Standalone Addons: Individual, decoupled expansion modules covering animated attributes, component styling, hierarchy design, automated validation, visual inspector customization, and advanced developer tooling (ToolBox Vol. 1).
  4. MSUltimate Pro (Full Collection): The flagship all-in-one bundle containing the entire ecosystem—Core, all 6 Addons, 4 developer tools, complete C# source code, and the centralized test suite (573 test files / 3,275 test methods / 6,115 test cases) at a massive bundle discount.

3. Detailed Package Breakdown

🆓 MSUltimate Core (Community Edition)

The modern inspector standard for every indie developer.

  • Price: Free
  • Format: Precompiled, high-performance obfuscated DLLs.
  • Audience: Solo developers, students, educators, and indie game studios with gross annual revenue under $200,000 USD.
  • Key Capabilities:
    • 156+ Core Attributes: Complete access to layout groups ([BoxGroup], [BeginTabGroup] / [EndTabGroup], [BeginSplitPane] / [EndSplitPane]), smart conditionals ([ShowIf], [EnableIf]), buttons ([Button], [ToolbarToggle]), specialized pickers ([MinMaxSlider], [ValueDropdown]), in-scene 3D handles, and reactive callbacks ([OnValueChanged]).
    • Custom Serializers: Native Unity serialization for SerializableDictionary<TKey, TValue>, SerializableHashSet<T>, SerializableMatrix2D<T>, SerializableMatrix3D<T>, SerializableQueue<T>, and SerializableStack<T> via ISerializationCallbackReceiver.
    • Extended Data Types: Integrated visual drawers for SerializableNullable<T>, SerializableDateTime, SerializableRange<T>, SerializableTuple<T1, T2> / SerializableTuple<T1, T2, T3>, and SerializableType.
    • Modular Window System: Turn any class or ScriptableObject into a standalone, dockable editor window with tree-based menus (ModularMenuEditorWindow) and modal dialogs.
    • Zero Boilerplate Collection Cascading: Decorate items inside List<T>, arrays T[], and dictionaries seamlessly.

MSUltimate Core (Pro Edition)

Unrestricted core power for commercial game studios.

  • Price: $149.99
  • Format: 100% Clean, modular C# Source Code.
  • Audience: Studios and professional teams requiring uncompiled source access for custom engine extensions, internal tooling integrations, and source control auditing.
  • Key Capabilities:
    • Everything included in the Community Edition.
    • Full C# Source Code: Direct access to all core drawers, layout processors, and reflection engines.
    • No Revenue Ceilings: Fully commercial license with zero financial thresholds or upgrade obligations.
    • Dedicated Engineering Support: Direct email support with core framework architects.

MSUltimate Pro (Full Collection)

The complete AAA development suite at maximum bundle savings.

  • Price: 299.99 *(Over350 in combined standalone value)*
  • Format: Complete C# Source Code for Core and ALL 6 Official Addons.
  • Audience: Professional studios, technical artists, and tool developers who want the definitive, all-in-one Unity authoring environment.
  • What's Included:
    • MSUltimate Core (Pro): Full source code for all 156+ core attributes, serializers, types, and window systems.
    • All 6 Official Addons: Animated Attributes, Component Designer, Hierarchy Designer, Validation Module, Inspector Customizer, and ToolBox Vol. 1.
    • 454+ Concrete Attributes (463 Total Attribute Classes): Exhaustive coverage across Core and Addons.
    • 4 Standalone Developer Tools: Advanced Console, History Track, Object Lifetime Tracker, and Live Track.
    • Centralized Test Suite: 573 test files containing 3,275 [Test]/[UnityTest] methods (6,115 total test cases including [TestCase]) verifying attribute lifecycles, UI Toolkit visual tree safety, and collection cascading.
    • VIP Priority Support: Direct channel access for fast issue resolution and roadmap feature requests.

4. The 6 Standalone Addons (A La Carte Modules)

Each official Addon is engineered to be 100% decoupled—it can be purchased and imported individually to solve a specific development challenge without requiring the full suite:

TEXT
MSUltimate Ecosystem
 ├── Core Framework (Free Community or Pro Source)
 │    │
 │    ├── [Visuals]     ───► MSUltimate - Component Designer
 │    ├── [Motion]      ───► MSUltimate - Animated Attributes
 │    ├── [Structure]   ───► MSUltimate - Hierarchy Designer
 │    ├── [Integrity]   ───► MSUltimate - Validation Module
 │    ├── [Customizing] ───► MSUltimate - Inspector Customizer
 │    └── [Diagnostics] ───► MSUltimate - ToolBox Vol. 1

1. MSUltimate - Animated Attributes ($29.99)

  • Focus: Micro-interactions, animated telemetry, and sensory feedback.
  • Content: 99 concrete attributes (101 attribute classes including base contracts) across 12 runtime categories (13 documentation folders).
  • Highlights: Dynamic combat HUD meters ([BossHealthBar], [ManaShieldBubble], [CombatComboCounter]), sci-fi data visualizers ([HexGridMatrix], [HologramFlicker], [SonarPingWave]), particle simulations ([ParticleBurst], [ElectricArcSparks]), and kinetic typography ([GlitchChopText], [NeonSignFlicker]).

2. MSUltimate - Component Designer ($29.99)

  • Focus: AAA MonoBehaviour Inspector card aesthetics and branded component presentation.
  • Content: 74 concrete attributes (75 attribute classes including ComponentAttribute) across 7 categories.
  • Highlights: Styled component borders and backgrounds ([ComponentBorder], [ComponentBackground], [ComponentColorStrip]), atmospheric VFX ([ComponentParticles], [ComponentAuroraEffect], [ComponentCircuitFlow]), header controls ([ComponentHeader], [ComponentHeaderButton]), and genre themes ([ComponentBlueprint], [ComponentSciFiHUD], [ComponentRPGStatCard]).

3. MSUltimate - Hierarchy Designer ($29.99)

  • Focus: Complete organizational overhaul of the Unity Scene Hierarchy window.
  • Content: 82 concrete attributes (83 attribute classes including HierarchyAttribute) across 8 categories.
  • Highlights: Virtual colored folders ([HierarchyFolder]), branching tree connector lines ([HierarchyTreeBranch]), live hierarchy telemetry widgets ([HierarchyAudioMonitor], [HierarchyLightVisualizer], [HierarchyComponentIcons], [HierarchyEventHookTracker]), active/lock toggles ([HierarchyActiveButton], [HierarchyLock]), component counters, and performance badges ([HierarchyDrawCallTracker], [HierarchyPolyCount], [HierarchyMemoryTracker]).

4. MSUltimate - Validation Module ($29.99)

  • Focus: Real-time data integrity and project-wide asset/scene scanning.
  • Content: 39 validation attributes + dedicated ValidationWindow + ValidationCLI + extensible IValidationRule / IDeepValidationRule pipelines.
  • Highlights: Real-time field assertions ([ValidateComponent], [ValidateAssetPath], [ValidateNotNull], [ValidateRange], [ValidateTextureSize]), paired with a project-wide scan window that detects broken object/asset/prefab/shader/event references and offers 1-click auto-fix for supported deep rules (missing scripts, empty GameObjects, disabled root objects, abnormal scale, missing AudioSource clips, non-convex MeshColliders, unnecessary raycast targets, and useless lights).

5. MSUltimate - Inspector Customizer ($39.99)

  • Focus: Non-destructive visual inspector styling, Makeover Graph, AI Decorator, and C# code baking.
  • Content: InspectorCustomizerWindow, 30-node MakeoverGraphWindow, AIDecoratorModalWindow, TemplateRecipeManagerWindow, ComponentDefaultsWindow, InspectorMakeoverCompareWindow, and AttributeCodeBaker.
  • Highlights: Apply, reorder, and tune MSUltimate attributes visually via InspectorProfile assets with zero script changes, author node-based makeover rules and .msmakomacro subgraphs, generate layouts with Multi-LLM AI + local privacy scrubbing, preview live before/after diffs, and bake overrides cleanly back into C# source code.

6. MSUltimate - ToolBox Vol. 1 ($44.99)

  • Focus: High-throughput developer diagnostics and runtime telemetry.
  • Content: 4 standalone tools + 4 tracking attributes ([ConsoleCommand], [HistoryTrack], [TrackLifetime], [LiveTrack]).
  • Highlights:
    • Advanced Console: High-speed log filtering, rule alerts, callstack analysis, runtime UI Toolkit overlay, and [ConsoleCommand] console commands.
    • History Track: Timeline-based Undo/Redo state inspection, variable change diffs, and Play Mode tweak committing.
    • Object Lifetime Tracker: Allocation tracking, dangling C# reference hunting, scene teardown leak detection, and GameObject lifecycle auditing.
    • Live Track: In-SceneView floating telemetry HUD and multi-scale oscilloscope variable graphs.

Choose MSUltimate Core (Community) if:

  • You are an indie developer, hobbyist, student, or startup with under $200K USD annual revenue.
  • You want an immediate, massive upgrade to the default Unity Inspector with zero financial investment.
  • You want 156+ battle-tested attributes, custom serializers, and windowing tools in a clean, drop-in DLL package.

Choose MSUltimate Core (Pro) if:

  • Your studio earns more than $200K USD annually or requires uncompiled C# source code.
  • You need to customize drawer internals or integrate private tooling hooks into your internal engine pipeline.
  • You only need the foundational inspector framework and serializers without the extra styling or diagnostics addons.

Choose MSUltimate Pro (Full Collection) if:

  • You want the complete, ultimate development experience with all 454+ attributes, 6 addons, and 4 developer tools.
  • You want continuous integration (CI) safety backed by the official 573-file / 6,115-case automated test suite.
  • You want maximum cost efficiency (saves over $100 compared to buying packages individually).

Choose Individual Addons if:

  • You already have an established inspector workflow, but specifically need hierarchy organization (Hierarchy Designer), scene validation (Validation Module), or advanced diagnostics (ToolBox Vol. 1).

6. Technical Specifications & Requirements

  • Unity Editor Version: Unity 6 (6000.x) and newer.
  • Render Pipelines: 100% compatible with Universal Render Pipeline (URP), High Definition Render Pipeline (HDRP), and Built-in Render Pipeline (BiRP).
  • Runtime Platforms: Windows, macOS, Linux, iOS, Android, WebGL, Xbox, PlayStation, Nintendo Switch. (All editor tooling code is editor-only and automatically stripped from runtime player builds).
  • Architecture: Native UI Toolkit with IMGUI compatibility layer. Zero runtime Garbage Collection (GC) allocations.

7. Licensing & Fair Use Summary

  • Community Edition: Free to use for commercial and non-commercial games by creators and studios with annual gross revenues and funding below $200,000 USD under our dedicated Custom License. If your revenue or capital funding exceeds this threshold, upgrading to a Pro license is required.
  • Pro Editions & Addons: Governed by the standard Unity Asset Store End User License Agreement (EULA) on a per-seat basis (one license required per developer seat utilizing the software in your studio), with no gross revenue ceilings or royalty obligations.
  • Redistribution Policy: Redistribution, sublicensing, decompilation, reverse engineering, or hosting on public repositories is strictly prohibited across all editions.

Need help deciding or have questions about custom studio licensing? Reach out to our team at maharajastudiocustomerservice@gmail.com or join our Discord Community.

Core Framework/Groups & Layouts/[AdvancedClass]

[AdvancedClass]

Renders serialized structs and classes as sleek, structured inspector cards featuring real-time search, pagination, foldouts, and accent bars.

1. Overview & Value Proposition

What it does: Transforms plain serialized classes and structs into modern card panels with customizable headers, collapsible foldouts, left accent bars, real-time search filtering, and pagination for massive data structures.

The Problem: In standard Unity, complex serialized structs or nested classes (such as player stats, weapon specs, or AI brain nodes) render as flat, indented blocks. As data structures grow, they clutter the inspector, make finding specific fields difficult, and lack clear visual boundaries between parent and child data.

The Solution: Add [AdvancedClass] to any serialized class or struct field:

  • Card Framing & Headers: Wraps all inner fields within a styled container with custom borders, rounded corners, and headers.
  • Collapsible Foldout: Toggle collapse/expansion (IsFoldable, StartExpanded) with field count badges (ShowFieldCount = true).
  • Real-Time Search Bar: Instantly filter inner fields by name with ShowSearch = true.
  • Built-In Pagination: Cleanly paginate massive structures (ShowPagination = true, ItemsPerPage = 10).
  • Visual Ergonomics: Left accent bars, alternating row colors, field separators, and custom padding.

2. Quick Start

csharp
using System;
using UnityEngine;
using MaharajaStudio.MSUltimate.Runtime;

[Serializable]
public class CharacterStats
{
    public int strength = 18;
    public int agility = 14;
    public int intelligence = 22;
    public float criticalChance = 0.15f;
}

public class HeroEntity : MonoBehaviour
{
    [AdvancedClass(HeaderLabel = "RPG Core Attributes", AccentBarColor = "#3498db", ShowFieldCount = true)]
    public CharacterStats attributes;
}

Core Framework/Groups & Layouts/[AdvancedList]

[AdvancedList]

Supercharges Arrays and Lists with drag-and-drop reordering, instant search filtering, pagination, item counts, and lifecycle event callbacks.

1. Overview & Value Proposition

What it does: Replaces Unity's standard ReorderableList with an advanced, feature-rich collection container. Adds live search filtering, pagination for long lists, expand/collapse controls, dynamic element labeling, and C# event hooks for add/remove operations.

The Problem: Standard Unity lists become unwieldy when collections hold more than 10–20 elements. Finding specific items requires scrolling through dozens of rows, there are no search tools or pagination, reordering laggy elements is frustrating, and running logic when items are added or removed requires tedious OnValidate reflection.

The Solution: Add [AdvancedList] to any array or list field:

  • Real-Time Search Bar: Filter list elements on the fly by text, name, or properties.
  • Built-In Pagination: Paginate large lists with customizable page sizes (ItemsPerPage = 10), keeping the inspector compact.
  • Dynamic Element Titles: Name element headers using member properties (OnTitleAttribute = "enemyName").
  • Expand / Collapse All: 1-click toolbar buttons to expand or collapse all elements at once.
  • Lifecycle Callbacks: Trigger custom methods when items are added or deleted (OnItemAdded, OnItemRemoved).

2. Quick Start

csharp
using System.Collections.Generic;
using UnityEngine;
using MaharajaStudio.MSUltimate.Runtime;

public class InventoryRoster : MonoBehaviour
{
    [AdvancedList(ShowSearch = true, ShowPagination = true, ItemsPerPage = 5)]
    public List<string> playerInventory = new List<string>
    {
        "Health Potion", "Iron Sword", "Mana Elixir", "Shield of Valor",
        "Torch", "Golden Key", "Leather Armor", "Boots of Speed"
    };
}

Core Framework/Groups & Layouts/[BeginHorizontal]

[BeginHorizontal]

Starts an imperative horizontal layout row placing subsequent inspector fields, properties, or buttons side-by-side until closed by [EndHorizontal].

1. Overview & Value Proposition

What it does: Opens an imperative horizontal layout scope in the Inspector. All subsequent serialized fields, properties, or methods decorated up until an [EndHorizontal] attribute are laid out horizontally in a single row or flexbox grid with customizable spacing, borders, titles, and alignments.

The Problem: By default, Unity stacks every single serialized field vertically, consuming massive amounts of vertical screen space. For tight groupings of related controls—such as Min/Max bounds, paired multipliers, or a row of utility buttons—vertical stacking feels clunky and requires continuous scrolling.

The Solution: Add [BeginHorizontal] before the first field and [EndHorizontal] after the last:

  • Side-by-Side Ergonomics: Renders multiple controls in a compact horizontal row.
  • Flexbox-Style Layout: Full control over Gap, FlexGrow, AlignItems, and JustifyContent.
  • Responsive Label Modes: Adjust LayoutMode (AdaptiveInline, ResponsiveStack, AlwaysStacked) and LabelWidth to fit narrow inspector windows.
  • Card Framing & Headers: Wrap the row in a border box (Box = true), add header titles (Title), or make it collapsible (Collapsible = true).

2. Quick Start

csharp
using UnityEngine;
using MaharajaStudio.MSUltimate.Runtime;

public class MovementSettings : MonoBehaviour
{
    [BeginHorizontal(Gap = 8f)]
    public float walkSpeed = 4.5f;

    [EndHorizontal]
    public float runSpeed = 9.0f;
}

Core Framework/Groups & Layouts/[BeginSplitPane]

[BeginSplitPane]

Divides the Inspector into two resizable panes (left/right or top/bottom) with interactive dragging, custom headers, and minimum size constraints.

1. Overview & Value Proposition

What it does: Opens a dual-pane resizable layout container in the Inspector. Divides controls into two distinct regions (Pane 1 and Pane 2) separated by a draggable splitter handle. Fields declared after the initial [BeginSplitPane] populate Pane 1. A second [BeginSplitPane("GroupName")] switches into Pane 2, and [EndSplitPane] seals the dual-pane container so subsequent members return to standard full-width layout flow.

The Problem: Complex components—such as character setup workbenches, inventory managers, or dialogue editors—often benefit from master-detail workflows (e.g. list of items on the left, properties of the selected item on the right). Standard Unity inspectors only support one vertical column, forcing endless scrolling between lists and item details.

The Solution: Add [BeginSplitPane("GroupName")] paired with a second [BeginSplitPane("GroupName")] and [EndSplitPane]:

  • Interactive Splitter: Draggable separator handle with customizable hover effects, thickness, and margin.
  • Horizontal & Vertical Split: Supports side-by-side (UiOrientation.Horizontal) or stacked dual panes (UiOrientation.Vertical).
  • Independent Scrolling & Minimum Sizes: Protect panes from collapsing below readable limits via PaneMinSize, Pane1ScrollMode, and Pane2ScrollMode.
  • Custom Pane Titles & Cards: Decorate each pane with its own title header, icon, background colors, and border styling.
  • Collapsible Panes: Enable 1-click collapse arrows on either pane via ShowCollapseButtons, Pane1Collapsible, or Pane2Collapsible.

2. Quick Start

csharp
using UnityEngine;
using MaharajaStudio.MSUltimate.Runtime;

public class MasterDetailInspector : MonoBehaviour
{
    // Pane 1: Master Overview
    [BeginSplitPane("CharacterSplit", InitialSplitterPosition = 180f)]
    public string characterName = "Knight";
    public int characterLevel = 10;

    // Pane 2: Detail Properties
    [BeginSplitPane("CharacterSplit")] // Switches to Pane 2
    public int healthPoints = 100;
    [EndSplitPane]
    public int manaPoints = 50;

    // Renders full-width below the split pane
    public bool isHeroic = true;
}

Core Framework/Groups & Layouts/[BeginTabGroup]

[BeginTabGroup]

Organizes inspector members into an interactive multi-tab navigation bar with custom tab icons, active indicator bars, and theme styling.

1. Overview & Value Proposition

What it does: Initializes an interactive tabbed navigation layout. Subsequent serialized members are grouped under the specified tab button until closed by an [EndTabGroup] or transitioned to another tab in the same group. Multiple declarations sharing the same GroupName automatically fuse into a unified tab strip.

The Problem: Complex gameplay components—such as player controllers, AI behavior trees, or vehicle physics—often contain dozens of fields. Stacking all fields vertically creates endless inspector scrollbars and overwhelms designers trying to locate specific features.

The Solution: Add [BeginTabGroup("TabName")] across your class:

  • Clean Tab Switching: Switch seamlessly between tabs like "General", "Movement", "Combat", and "VFX".
  • Tab Icons & Visual Indicators: Decorate tabs with built-in Unity icons (TabIcon) and colored bottom/top indicator lines (ShowTabIndicator = true).
  • Shared Group Identification: Tabs sharing the same GroupName coalesce into a single unified tab container.
  • Collapsible Tab Sets: Make the entire tab container collapsible with Collapsible = true.
  • Exhaustive Styling Engine: Customize colors, borders, fonts, paddings, and hover effects for both the tab strip and the content body.

2. Quick Start

csharp
using UnityEngine;
using MaharajaStudio.MSUltimate.Runtime;

public class PlayerController : MonoBehaviour
{
    // Tab 1: Locomotion
    [BeginTabGroup("Locomotion", GroupName = "PlayerTabs")]
    public float walkSpeed = 5f;
    public float sprintSpeed = 10f;

    // Tab 2: Combat
    [BeginTabGroup("Combat", GroupName = "PlayerTabs")]
    public int maxHealth = 100;
    [EndTabGroup] // Placed on the final field of the tab group to close it
    public float attackPower = 25f;

    // Renders full-width below the tab container
    public bool isPlayerActive = true;
}

Core Framework/Groups & Layouts/[BoxGroup]

[BoxGroup]

Groups fields, properties, and methods into a framed inspector box with styled headers, custom background fills, and borders.

1. Overview & Value Proposition

What it does: Encloses related serialized fields, properties, and buttons inside a styled, framed box container with a distinct header bar. All members sharing the same groupName are clustered together automatically into the same visual card.

The Problem: Standard Unity inspectors display hundreds of properties in an endless uninterrupted gray list. Without clear visual boundaries, related parameters (such as movement speeds, stamina costs, or audio settings) bleed together, resulting in cognitive fatigue and accidental parameter mistakes.

The Solution: Add [BoxGroup("GroupName")] to any member:

  • Automatic Member Grouping: Decorate multiple fields with the same group name to automatically gather them into a single container.
  • Custom Header Styling: Customize header labels, font sizes, colors, alignments, and backgrounds.
  • Framed Card Aesthetics: Adjust border widths, border colors, corner radii, and body background colors to match your studio's design language.
  • Method & Button Support: Group utility methods alongside the variables they manipulate.

What it does: Gathers multiple methods marked as inspector buttons into a unified, aligned button group. Methods sharing the same groupName are placed together in a horizontal button strip or vertical stack, ensuring equal button widths, uniform heights, and shared headers.

The Problem: In standard inspector tools, adding multiple buttons to a MonoBehaviour creates large, bulky full-width buttons stacked vertically on top of one another.   • Unified Toolbar Rows: Places related buttons side-by-side in a sleek, compact toolbar.

  • Flexible Orientations: Supports horizontal toolbars (UiOrientation.Horizontal) or vertical column clusters (UiOrientation.Vertical).
  • Card Framing & Titles: Optional surrounding border box (Box = true) and group title header with icons.

Core Framework/Groups & Layouts/[EndHorizontal]

[EndHorizontal]

Terminates an active imperative horizontal layout row started by [BeginHorizontal], restoring subsequent members to vertical stacking.

1. Overview & Value Proposition

What it does: Acts as the closing scope delimiter for imperative horizontal layout rows initiated by [BeginHorizontal]. All members declared between [BeginHorizontal] and the ending boundary are rendered side-by-side in a horizontal row; subsequent members return to standard vertical layout flow.

The Problem: Imperative layout systems require unambiguous boundary markers. Without an explicit closing tag, an open horizontal row would swallow all following properties in the class, squishing them indefinitely into an unreadable horizontal line.

The Solution: Add [EndHorizontal] to terminate the row:

  • IncludeInGroup = true: Decorate the final member of the row; it will be included in the horizontal group before the scope closes.
  • IncludeInGroup = false (default): Decorate the first member outside the row; the horizontal scope closes immediately before this member is rendered, placing it cleanly below.
  • Nesting Support: Supports nested horizontal blocks inside outer cards, tab groups, or vertical stacks.

2. Quick Start

csharp
using UnityEngine;
using MaharajaStudio.MSUltimate.Runtime;

public class CoordinatesSetup : MonoBehaviour
{
    [BeginHorizontal]
    public float minX = 0f;

    // IncludeInGroup = true includes maxX in the horizontal row and then closes it
    [EndHorizontal(IncludeInGroup = true)]
    public float maxX = 100f;

    // Stacks normally in standard vertical layout below the row
    public float depthZ = 50f;
}

Core Framework/Groups & Layouts/[EndSplitPane]

[EndSplitPane]

Terminates an active dual-pane split layout scope started by [BeginSplitPane], restoring subsequent members to default layout flow.

1. Overview & Value Proposition

What it does: Closes the active dual-pane container scope opened by [BeginSplitPane]. All subsequent fields, properties, and methods declared after [EndSplitPane] are rendered outside the split container in standard full-width vertical layout flow.

The Problem: Without an explicit closing boundary, all fields declared below a split container would continue to be captured inside Pane 2, making it impossible to add full-width inspector sections (like global settings or master action buttons) below the split pane.

The Solution: Place [EndSplitPane] on the final member intended for Pane 2:

  • Clean Container Termination: Explicitly finishes the resizable split pane view after rendering the decorated member.
  • Post-Split Alignment: Subsequent members span the full width of the inspector window.
  • Robust Error Handling: Defensively recovers if nested incorrectly without throwing GUI exceptions.

Core Framework/Groups & Layouts/[EndTabGroup]

[EndTabGroup]

What it does: Acts as the closing scope delimiter for multi-tab layout groups opened with [BeginTabGroup]. Decorating the final member of a tab with [EndTabGroup] seals the tab container after rendering that member; all subsequent members in the script render outside the tab container across the full width of the inspector.

The Problem: Without an explicit tab delimiter, any field added to a MonoBehaviour would automatically be trapped inside the very last tab declared in the script. Placing global fields, master action buttons, or status banners below the tab view would be impossible.

  • Clean Scope Closure: Seals the tab container cleanly and resets layout state.
  • Global Footer Support: Allows adding full-width controls, reset buttons, and telemetry below the tab view.
  • Defensive Layout Recovery: Prevents GUI tree corruptions even if tab indices are mismatched.

Core Framework/Groups & Layouts/[HorizontalGroup]

[HorizontalGroup]

Declaratively groups fields, properties, or buttons side-by-side into a named horizontal row with explicit column widths and flexbox alignment.

1. Overview & Value Proposition

What it does: Declaratively aligns multiple serialized members side-by-side into a horizontal row. Unlike imperative [BeginHorizontal] / [EndHorizontal] pairs, [HorizontalGroup] works declaratively by clustering all members sharing the same groupName, with optional per-field column widths (Width).

The Problem: Placing multiple related properties on the same line (such as X/Y offsets, Min/Max thresholds, or paired health and mana bars) using standard Unity requires custom property drawers or awkward GUI code.

The Solution: Add [HorizontalGroup("GroupName")] to any member:

  • Declarative Grouping: Simply assign the same group name; MSUltimate automatically forms the row without requiring ending tags.
  • Explicit Column Widths: Pass pixel widths (e.g. 120f) or proportional flex fractions (0.5f) per column.
  • Flexbox Alignment: Control cross-axis alignment (AlignItems) and horizontal distribution (JustifyContent).
  • Responsive Label Control: Hide labels (HideLabel = true), set fixed label widths (LabelWidth), or configure responsive vertical stacking (LayoutMode).

2. Quick Start

    public float minLimit = 0f;

}

Core Framework/Groups & Layouts/[LabelLayout]

[LabelLayout]

Advanced label and input control layout modifier providing granular control over label positioning, adaptive inline fitting, responsive auto-stacking breakpoints, and input constraints.

1. Overview & Value Proposition

What it does: [LabelLayout] dynamically alters how field labels and their corresponding input fields are positioned, sized, and rendered in the Unity Inspector. It supports adaptive inline auto-sizing (removing awkward blank gaps), responsive auto-stacking (switching from horizontal to vertical layout below a custom width breakpoint), permanent vertical stacking, and explicit label sizing constraints.

The Problem: Standard Unity Inspectors use rigid, fixed-width columns for property labels. In narrow inspector panels or multi-column layouts ([HorizontalGroup], split panes, grids), this rigid width causes long labels to be brutally truncated while input fields collapse into unusable slivers. Conversely, short labels ("X", "HP", "ID") leave massive empty gaps before their input boxes.

The Solution: Applying [LabelLayout] gives developers complete control over field ergonomics:

  • Adaptive Inline Auto-Fitting (AdaptiveInline): Dynamically measures label text length and pulls the input field directly alongside it with a tight, configurable gap.
  • Responsive Auto-Stacking (ResponsiveStack): Displays fields inline on wide screens, but seamlessly transitions to vertical stacking (label on top, full-width input below) whenever inspector column width drops below a configurable pixel breakpoint.
  • Always Stacked Layout (AlwaysStacked): Perfect for multi-column weapon stats or telemetry tables where labels sit cleanly above full-width inputs.
  • Auto-Hide on Compact Views (AutoHideLabel): Automatically hides the text label in super-narrow slots, giving 100% of the horizontal space to the input field.

2. Quick Start

csharp
using UnityEngine;
using MaharajaStudio.MSUltimate.Runtime;

public class CombatUnit : MonoBehaviour
{
    // Auto-sizes label to fit text without wasting horizontal space
    [LabelLayout(LabelLayoutMode.AdaptiveInline)]
    public float hp = 100f;

    // Automatically stacks vertically if column width drops below 200px
    [LabelLayout(LabelLayoutMode.ResponsiveStack, breakpoint: 200f)]
    public Vector3 spawnAnchor;
}

Core Framework/Groups & Layouts/[TableList]

[TableList]

Renders lists and arrays as a spreadsheet-style interactive table where object properties map directly to horizontal columns.

1. Overview & Value Proposition

What it does: Transforms standard serialized lists or arrays of custom classes/structs into a structured data grid. Instead of repetitive nested foldouts for each element, each serialized field becomes a table column, and each list item becomes a compact row.

The Problem: Managing collections of structured data (like weapon inventories, loot drop tables, or enemy spawn waves) using Unity's default list view is tedious. Every element has its own foldout that must be clicked open, wasting screen real estate and making side-by-side data comparison impossible.

The Solution: Add [TableList] to any list or array field:

  • Spreadsheet-Style Grid: View all items and compare their stats side-by-side in clean horizontal rows.
  • Column Header Row: Auto-generates column headers matching member property names.
  • Zebra Striping: Alternating row background colors for effortless horizontal eye tracking.
  • Scroll Capping: Set MaxHeight to constrain massive lists inside a scrollable table pane.

2. Quick Start

csharp
using System;
using System.Collections.Generic;
using UnityEngine;
using MaharajaStudio.MSUltimate.Runtime;

[Serializable]
public class ItemDrop
{
    public string itemId;
    [Range(0f, 1f)]

    public int minQuantity;
    public int maxQuantity;
}

public class LootTable : MonoBehaviour
{
    [TableList]
    public List<ItemDrop> drops = new List<ItemDrop>();
}

[VerticalGroup]

The Problem: Creating balanced multi-column layouts (such as Column 1: Equipment, Column 2: Stats, Column 3: Actions) in Unity inspectors is nearly impossible with standard tools. Fields either stack linearly or get squished across unorganized horizontal rows.

  • Collapsible Columns: Collapse individual vertical panels on demand (Collapsible = true).
  • Flexible Spacing, Separators & Scrolling: Add horizontal separator lines between child items, enable vertical scrolling with Scrollable = true, or indent sub-blocks via IndentLevel.

Core Framework/Conditional Visibility Index

Conditional Visibility

The next-generation dynamic inspector logic framework for Unity.
Control the visibility, interactivity, read-only locking, and state of fields, groups, and action buttons using boolean flags, compound C#-style inline expressions, parameterized method validators, bitwise flag operations, engine state macros, and relative parent traversal.

1. Quick Decision Matrix: What to Use When

GoalRecommended AttributeVisual ResultTypical Use Case
Reveal field only when setting is enabled[ShowIf]Collapses / expands fieldHiding secondary settings (e.g. show burstCount only when fireMode == Burst).
Hide field when setting is active[HideIf]Completely hides fieldHiding healthPoints when isInvincible or godMode is toggled.
Keep visible but grey out (disable editing)[EnableIf] / [DisableIf]Greys out (read-only opacity)Showing a locked feature with a tooltip explaining required unlock level.
Dynamic read-only styling with color tint[ReadOnlyConditional]Read-only with custom opacity & color tintLocking weapon configs during active combat or runtime play mode.
Multi-condition logic with animation & transitions[ConditionalField]Fade animation + AND/OR condition arraysAdvanced setup requiring animated fade transitions and multi-condition arrays.
Conditionally enable/disable Inspector buttons[ButtonConditional]Greys out action buttonDisabling "Respawn" when player is already alive.

2. Supported Condition Syntax & Evaluator Capabilities

The MSUltimate conditional engine evaluates condition strings seamlessly across all conditional attributes ([ShowIf], [HideIf], [EnableIf], [DisableIf], [ConditionalField], [ReadOnlyConditional], and [ButtonConditional]).

You are never restricted to simple boolean fields. The engine natively supports:

TEXT
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                        MSUltimate Condition Engine                     │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  1. Simple Members        →  [ShowIf("isGrounded")]                    │
│  2. Operator Comparison   →  [ShowIf("level", 10, GreaterThanOrEqual)] │
│  3. Inline C# Expressions →  [ShowIf("$health > 50 && $shield <= 0")]  │
│  4. Parameterized Methods →  [ShowIf("HasPermission('Admin')")]        │
│  5. Bitwise Flag Masks    →  [ShowIf("flags", MyFlags.A, HasFlag)]     │
│  6. Global Engine Macros  →  [ShowIf("@isPlayMode")]                   │
│  7. Relative Traversal    →  [ShowIf("$parent.enableAdvanced")]        │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Syntax 1: Simple Identifier (Field, Property, or Method)

Pass the name of any bool field, property (including auto-properties and expression-bodied getters), or parameterless method.

csharp
public bool enableAdvanced;
public bool IsAlive => currentHealth > 0;
public bool CheckIsGrounded() => characterController.isGrounded;

[ShowIf("enableAdvanced")]
public float customMultiplier = 1.5f;

[ShowIf("IsAlive")]
public int ammoCount = 30;

[ShowIf("CheckIsGrounded")]
public float jumpForce = 8.5f;

Syntax 2: Direct Comparison Operators

Compare any field or property against an explicit target value using ConditionOperator.

csharp
public WeaponType weaponType = WeaponType.Ranged;
public int characterLevel = 5;

// Enum matching
[ShowIf("weaponType", WeaponType.Ranged)]
public int arrowCapacity = 40;

// Numeric relational comparison
[ShowIf("characterLevel", 10, ConditionOperator.GreaterThanOrEqual)]
public string masterPerk = "Blade Dance";

Supported Operators in ConditionOperator:

  • Equals (default)
  • NotEquals
  • GreaterThan
  • LessThan
  • GreaterThanOrEqual
  • LessThanOrEqual
  • HasFlag (for [System.Flags] enum bitmasks)

Syntax 3: Inline C#-Style Expressions (Mini-Parser)

Write natural compound boolean expressions directly inside the attribute string with zero boilerplate helper properties.

  • Prefix variable names with $ (optional if unambiguous) or use direct member names.
  • Combine conditions with logical operators: && (AND), || (OR), ! (NOT).
  • Group operations using parentheses: (A || B) && C.
  • Compare against numbers, string literals ('Admin'), enum values, booleans (true/false), and null.
csharp
public float health = 75f;
public float shield = 0f;
public WeaponMode weaponMode = WeaponMode.Burst;
public bool isInvincible = false;

// Compound logical expression with grouping
[ShowIf("$health > 50 && $shield <= 0")]
public string berserkAura = "Crimson Fury";

// Enum comparison inside expression
[ShowIf("$weaponMode == WeaponMode.Burst")]
public int burstCount = 3;

// Complex relational grouping with negation
[ShowIf("($health < 25 || $shield <= 0) && !$isInvincible")]
public Color lowHealthAlertColor = Color.red;

Syntax 4: Parameterized Method Invocations

Validator methods can accept literal arguments directly from the attribute condition string. This allows a single reusable validator method to power dozens of fields with different parameters.

csharp
// Single method serves multiple different fields
[ShowIf("HasPermission('Admin')")]
public string adminSecretCode = "ADM-994";

[ShowIf("HasPermission('Moderator')")]
public string banReason = "Rule violation";

[EnableIf("ValidateLevel(20, false)")]
public GameObject highTierWeaponPrefab;

// In the same class:
public bool HasPermission(string requiredRole)
{
    return currentUserRole == requiredRole;
}

public bool ValidateLevel(int minLevel, bool allowVip)
{
    return playerLevel >= minLevel || (allowVip && isVipUser);
}

Syntax 5: Bitwise Flag Operations (HasFlag)

Test [System.Flags] bitmasks natively using ConditionOperator.HasFlag. Works with either enum instances or string flag names.

csharp
[System.Flags]
public enum CombatElements
{
    None = 0,
    Fire = 1 << 0,
    Ice = 1 << 1,
    Lightning = 1 << 2,
    Void = 1 << 3
}

public CombatElements activeElements = CombatElements.Fire | CombatElements.Lightning;

// Reveals when the 'Fire' bit is set
[ShowIf("activeElements", CombatElements.Fire, ConditionOperator.HasFlag)]
public float burnDuration = 5.0f;

// Reveals when the 'Void' bit is set
[ShowIf("activeElements", CombatElements.Void, ConditionOperator.HasFlag)]
public float voidRiftMultiplier = 2.5f;

Syntax 6: Global Context & Engine State Macros (@ Prefixes)

Built-in engine state macros that evaluate dynamically without declaring local dummy variables.

Engine MacroEvaluates True WhenTypical Use Case
@isPlayModeApplication.isPlaying == trueLive telemetry, frame graphs, debug buttons.
@isEditorRunning in Unity EditorEditor-only dev settings and gizmo controls.
@isPrefabStageEditing inside Prefab Isolation StageHiding scene-specific spawn nodes when editing prefabs.
@selectionCount == 1Exactly 1 GameObject is selectedDisabling complex drawers during multi-object editing.
@isProSkinUnity dark theme is activeTheme-dependent styling tweaks.
csharp
// Only visible in Play Mode
[ShowIf("@isPlayMode")]
public string liveFpsMonitor = "60 FPS";

// Hides when editing inside Prefab Isolation stage
[HideIf("@isPrefabStage")]
public GameObject sceneSpawnAnchor;

// Disables when multi-selecting multiple objects
[EnableIf("@selectionCount == 1")]
public string uniqueAssetId = "ID-001";

Syntax 7: Sibling & Parent Relative Traversal ($parent / ../)

Modular nested classes, sub-ScriptableObjects, or polymorphic [SerializeReference] nodes can read conditions from their parent container.

csharp
[System.Serializable]
public class ModularAudioSettings
{
    // Reads 'enableAudioEngine' from the parent MonoBehaviour!
    [ShowIf("$parent.enableAudioEngine")]
    public float masterVolume = 1.0f;

    // Relative parent traversal using '../' syntax
    [ShowIf("../isProLicense")]
    public string spatialAudioPreset = "Dolby Atmos 7.1";
}

public class GameSettings : ModularMonoBehaviour
{
    public bool enableAudioEngine = true;
    public bool isProLicense = false;

    public ModularAudioSettings audioSettings;
}

3. Developer Diagnostics & Typo Resilience (Fuzzy Matching)

In older frameworks, misspelling a condition name (e.g. [ShowIf("isAliv")]) causes the field to fail silently and permanently hide, forcing developers to spend hours debugging typos.

In MSUltimate:

  1. If a condition member cannot be resolved, the framework calculates the Levenshtein edit distance against all available fields, properties, and methods on the target object.
  2. It outputs an actionable warning in the Unity Console with the exact suggested correction:
TEXT
   [MSUltimate] Condition member 'isAliv' not found on 'PlayerController'. Did you mean 'isAlive'?
  1. Warnings are session-deduplicated — they log once per missing member rather than spamming the console on every frame repaint.
  2. If an invalid condition is encountered, the inspector falls back defensively to safe rendering rather than throwing exceptions or breaking the UI.

4. Reactive Event-Driven Mode (Zero-Polling)

MSUltimate features a zero-overhead reactive evaluation architecture:

  • Property Tracking: Uses UI Toolkit's native TrackPropertyValue on both target properties and their condition siblings. When a designer toggles a checkbox or moves a slider, the conditional element updates on the exact same frame (0ms latency) without waiting for an update tick.
  • ChangeEvent Listeners: Listens to ChangeEvent<bool>, ChangeEvent<string>, ChangeEvent<int>, ChangeEvent<float>, and ChangeEvent<Enum>.
  • Hybrid Safety Scheduler: A lightweight 100ms background heartbeat automatically catches external script mutations and undo/redo operations.

5. Attribute Cheat Sheet

csharp

// 2. Inverted Visibility

// 3. Relational Comparison

// 4. Bitwise Flag

Core Framework/Conditional Visibility/[ButtonConditional]

[ButtonConditional]

Conditionally enables or disables an Inspector-drawn method action button based on runtime states, compound C#-style inline expressions, parameterized method validators, or engine state macros.

1. Overview & Value Proposition

What it does: Greys out and disables an Inspector [Button] when a condition is not met (such as only allowing execution in Play Mode, or requiring prerequisite setup).

The Problem: In standard Unity, Inspector buttons are either always clickable or not drawn at all. Clicking a "Fire Cannon" button when the game is not playing, or clicking "Spawn Boss" when a boss is already active, throws NullReferenceException errors, corrupts test data, and frustrates designers.

The Solution: Add [ButtonConditional] to your method alongside [Button]:

  • Safe Method Triggering: Automatically greys out the button when conditions are unsatisfied.
  • Inline C#-Style Expressions: Enable buttons based on compound formulas (e.g. [ButtonConditional("$isArenaActive && $currentEnemyCount == 0")]) without writing dummy boolean properties.
  • Engine State Guard: Ensure buttons can only be pressed in Play Mode using [ButtonConditional("@isPlayMode")].
  • Parameterized Methods: Gate buttons behind role or parameter checks ([ButtonConditional("HasRole('Developer')")]).
  • Custom Disabled Styling: Configure disabled opacity (DisabledOpacity = 0.35f) and disabled background color tinting (DisabledColor = "#333333").
  • Clear User Guidance: Prevents accidental clicks and invalid gameplay states during testing.

2. Quick Start

csharp
using UnityEngine;
using MaharajaStudio.MSUltimate.Runtime;

public class TurretLauncher : MonoBehaviour
{
    public bool hasAmmunition = true;

    // 1. Basic Boolean Condition
    [Button("Fire Turret")]
    [ButtonConditional(nameof(hasAmmunition))]
    public void FireTurret()
    {
        Debug.Log("Fired rocket!");
    }

    // 2. Play Mode Only Action Button
    [Button("Simulate Overload")]
    [ButtonConditional("@isPlayMode")]
    public void SimulateOverload()
    {
        Debug.Log("Overload simulated!");
    }
}

    [Button("Refill Mana Fountains", colorHex: "#3498DB")]

        Debug.Log("[BossArena] Dev Purge complete!");

Core Framework/Conditional Visibility/[ConditionalField]

[ConditionalField]

Universal conditional visibility and interactivity attribute supporting compound C#-style inline expressions, multi-condition logic (AND/OR), bitwise flags, parameterized methods, smooth fade transitions, and disable-instead-of-hide modes.

1. Overview & Value Proposition

What it does: The cornerstone attribute of the conditional suite. Controls whether an Inspector field is visible or interactable based on single conditions, multi-condition arrays, inline C# expressions, comparison values, or bitmask flags.

The Problem: Inspectors quickly become overloaded with dozens of situational properties (e.g. showing "Homing Turn Rate" when trajectory is set to "Linear", or showing "Mana Cost" for pure melee warriors). Building custom editor drawers for every combination requires hundreds of lines of fragile GUI code.

The Solution: Add [ConditionalField] above any field, property, or method:

  • Universal Expression Engine: Write inline compound C# conditions ($score > 50 && $hasKey) directly in the attribute.
  • Parameterized Methods: Pass literal arguments into condition methods (CheckState(4, true)).
  • Bitwise Flag Masks (HasFlag): Test [System.Flags] enum bitmasks effortlessly with ConditionOperator.HasFlag.
  • Multi-Condition Arrays: Combine multiple flags with ConditionLogic.And or ConditionLogic.Or.
  • Engine State Macros: Built-in engine state macros (@isPlayMode, @isEditor, @isPrefabStage, @selectionCount).
  • Smooth Fade Animations: Fluid UI Toolkit transition animations (AnimateTransition = true).
  • Disable vs Hide Flexibility: Toggle between collapsing completely or greying out with custom opacity and disabled tooltips.
  • Zero-Polling Reactivity: Bound to UI Toolkit property changes for immediate 0ms updates.

2. Quick Start

csharp
using UnityEngine;
using MaharajaStudio.MSUltimate.Runtime;

public class AbilityConfig : MonoBehaviour
{
    public bool usesCooldown = true;

    // 1. Basic Boolean Toggle
    [ConditionalField(nameof(usesCooldown))]
    public float cooldownSeconds = 5.0f;

    // 2. Compound Inline Expression with DisableInsteadOfHide
    [ConditionalField("$usesCooldown && $cooldownSeconds > 10.0", DisableInsteadOfHide = true, DisabledTooltip = "Only active when cooldown exceeds 10s!")]
    public float cooldownReductionMultiplier = 0.8f;
}

csharp
using System;
using UnityEngine;
using MaharajaStudio.MSUltimate.Runtime;

public class ProjectileLauncher : ModularMonoBehaviour
{
    public enum TrajectoryType { Linear, Ballistic, Homing }

    [Flags]
    public enum ProjectileModifiers
    {
        None = 0,
        Piercing = 1 << 0,
        Explosive = 1 << 1,
        Bouncing = 1 << 2,
        LaserBeam = 1 << 3
    }

    [Header("Trajectory & Modifiers")]
    public TrajectoryType trajectory = TrajectoryType.Linear;
    public ProjectileModifiers modifiers = ProjectileModifiers.Piercing;
    public int upgradeTier = 1;
    public float energyCost = 25f;

    // 1. Direct Enum Match with Animated Fade
    [ConditionalField(nameof(trajectory), TrajectoryType.Homing, AnimateTransition = true, FadeDuration = 0.3f)]
    public float homingTurnRate = 180f;

    // 2. Bitwise HasFlag Evaluation
    [ConditionalField(nameof(modifiers), ProjectileModifiers.Explosive, ConditionOp = ConditionOperator.HasFlag)]
    public float explosionRadius = 4.5f;

    // 3. Multi-Condition Array (AND / OR)
    [ConditionalField(nameof(trajectory), Conditions = new[] { "trajectory", "upgradeTier" }, LogicOp = ConditionLogic.And)]
    [InfoBox("High Tier Ballistic Trajectory Active!")]
    public float gravityMultiplier = 1.2f;

    // 4. Compound Inline C# Expression
    [ConditionalField("$upgradeTier >= 3 && ($energyCost < 50 || $trajectory == TrajectoryType.Homing)")]
    [InfoBox("Overcharged Core: Unlocked when Tier >= 3 AND (Energy < 50 OR Homing is active)!")]
    public ParticleSystem overchargeEffect;

    // 5. Parameterized Method Invocation with DisableInsteadOfHide
    [ConditionalField("CanEquipSpecialAmmo('Plasma', 5)", DisableInsteadOfHide = true, DisabledTooltip = "Requires Upgrade Tier 5!")]
    public int plasmaCartridges = 10;

    // 6. Global Engine State Macro (@)
    [ConditionalField("@isPlayMode")]
    public string liveBallisticsMonitor = "Active Projectiles: 0";

    public bool CanEquipSpecialAmmo(string ammoType, int minTier)
    {
        return upgradeTier >= minTier;
    }
}

Core Framework/Conditional Visibility/[DisableIf]

[DisableIf]

Greys out and disables user interaction with a serialized field, property, or button when a specified condition evaluates to true.
Supports boolean flags, C#-style compound inline expressions, parameterized method calls, bitwise flags, engine macros, and relative parent traversal.

1. Overview & Value Proposition

What it does: Disables (greys out) a field so designers cannot edit it when conditions are met, while still keeping its current value clearly readable.

The Problem: Hiding a field completely can disorient game designers who wonder why a setting disappeared from the Inspector. In many design setups, you want the setting to remain visible for scannability and context, but prevent modifications when a master feature is toggled off or inactive.

The Solution: Add [DisableIf] above any serialized field, property, or button:

  • Preserve Context & Values: Fields remain visible with a clean greyed-out disabled style so team members can still inspect data.
  • Accidental Edit Protection: Prevents altering stats when prerequisites or sub-systems are inactive.
  • Inline C#-Style Expressions: Disable fields when multi-variable formulas evaluate to true ([DisableIf("$isInvulnerable || $maxHealth <= 0")]).
  • Parameterized Methods: Re-use a single validator across multiple fields ([DisableIf("IsRestrictedRole('Guest')")]).
  • Bitwise Flag Checking: Disable fields when specific bitmasks are active (ConditionOperator.HasFlag).
  • Engine State Macros: Lock fields dynamically during runtime play mode ([DisableIf("@isPlayMode")]).
  • Parent Relative Traversal: Modular child classes can disable fields based on parent state ([DisableIf("$parent.lockSettings")]).

    // 2. Compound Inline Expression
    [DisableIf("$isInfiniteAmmo || $maxMagazineCapacity <= 0")]

using System;
using UnityEngine;
using MaharajaStudio.MSUltimate.Runtime;

public class VehicleDrivetrain : ModularMonoBehaviour
{
    public enum TransmissionType { Automatic, Manual, Electric }

    [Flags]
    public enum EngineLocks
    {
        None = 0,
        Overheated = 1 << 0,
        MaintenanceMode = 1 << 1,
        EmergencyBrake = 1 << 2
    }

    [Header("Drivetrain Setup")]

    [DisableIf(nameof(activeLocks), EngineLocks.EmergencyBrake, ConditionOperator.HasFlag, DisabledTooltip = "Disabled while Emergency Brake is engaged!")]
    public float accelerationThrottle = 1.0f;

    public float nitrousBoostMultiplier = 2.0f;

    [DisableIf("@isPlayMode", DisabledTooltip = "Core tuning constants cannot be modified while Play Mode is running.")]
    public int baseGearRatio = 4;

    public bool IsLockActive(string lockName)
    {

    }

Core Framework/Conditional Visibility/[EnableIf]

[EnableIf]

Enables user interaction with a serialized field, property, or button only when a specified condition evaluates to true (greying it out otherwise).
Supports boolean flags, C#-style compound inline expressions, parameterized method calls, bitwise flags, engine macros, and relative parent traversal.

1. Overview & Value Proposition

What it does: Keeps a field visible in the Inspector but greys it out (read-only state) until a prerequisite setting or criteria is met.

The Problem: In standard Unity, secondary settings sit wide open for editing even when their parent feature is turned off. Game designers modify values that have zero actual effect, leading to phantom bug reports and frustration.

The Solution: Add [EnableIf] above dependent fields, properties, or methods:

  • Prerequisite Enforcement: Dependent fields stay visible so designers know they exist, but are interactively locked until unlocked.
  • Custom Disabled Tooltips: Inform designers exactly why a field is greyed out (e.g. DisabledTooltip = "Unlock at Level 10!").
  • Inline C#-Style Expressions: Enable fields based on compound logic ([EnableIf("$playerLevel >= 10 && $isLicensed")]).
  • Parameterized Methods: Re-use flexible validator methods with literal arguments ([EnableIf("HasPermission('Admin')")]).
  • Bitwise Flag Checking: Unlock fields when specific bitmasks are active (ConditionOperator.HasFlag).
  • Engine State Macros: Enable fields only when conditions match ([EnableIf("@selectionCount == 1")]).
  • Parent Relative Traversal: Modular child classes can read enable state from their parent ([EnableIf("$parent.allowEditing")]).

using System;

public class NetworkSyncManager : ModularMonoBehaviour
{
    [Flags]
    public enum LicenseFlags
    {
        None = 0,
        Standard = 1 << 0,

    [EnableIf(nameof(licenses), LicenseFlags.Enterprise, ConditionOperator.HasFlag, DisabledTooltip = "Requires Enterprise License!")]
    public int maxConcurrentPlayers = 10000;

    // 3. Compound Inline C# Expression
    [EnableIf("$isConnectedToCloud && $subscriptionTier >= 2")]
    [InfoBox("Live Sync: Enabled when Connected AND Tier >= 2!")]
    public float syncTickRateHz = 60.0f;

    // 4. Parameterized Method Invocation
    [EnableIf("HasRole('Administrator')")]
    public string debugServerToken = "SEC-TOKEN-ADMIN-4491";

    // 5. Global Context Engine Macro (@)
    [EnableIf("@selectionCount == 1", DisabledTooltip = "Disabled during multi-selection to prevent batch overwrite.")]
    public string uniqueInstanceId = "INST-GLOBAL-01";

    public bool HasRole(string requiredRole)
    {
        return requiredRole == "Administrator" && subscriptionTier >= 3;
    }

Core Framework/Conditional Visibility/[HideIf]

[HideIf]

Completely hides and collapses a serialized field, property, or method from the Inspector when a specified condition evaluates to true.
Supports boolean flags, C#-style compound inline expressions, parameterized method calls, bitwise flags, engine macros, and relative parent traversal.

1. Overview & Value Proposition

What it does: Removes irrelevant fields from view entirely when a condition is met, keeping your Inspector clean and focused on what matters right now.

The Problem: Complex game components frequently accumulate dozens of specialized fields (e.g. invulnerability toggles, god-mode overrides, platform-specific settings, debug logs). In standard Unity, secondary parameters always remain visible, leading to confusing layouts and cluttered inspectors.

The Solution: Add [HideIf] above fields, properties, or buttons:

  • Zero Screen Clutter: Collapses the entire field row, reclaiming vertical Inspector space.
  • Inline C#-Style Expressions: Hide fields when arbitrary formulas evaluate to true (e.g. [HideIf("$health <= 0 || $isDead")]).
  • Parameterized Methods: Re-use a single validator to hide fields based on argument criteria ([HideIf("IsRestrictedTier('Trial')")]).
  • Bitwise Flag Support: Hide fields when an enum bitmask flag is present (ConditionOperator.HasFlag).
  • Engine State Macros: Hide scene-specific fields when editing in isolation ([HideIf("@isPrefabStage")]).
  • Parent Relative Traversal: Hide fields in modular child objects based on parent settings ([HideIf("$parent.lockSettings")]).
  • Typo Protection: Misspelled condition names trigger actionable console warnings with suggestions rather than failing silently.

2. Quick Start

csharp
using UnityEngine;
using MaharajaStudio.MSUltimate.Runtime;

public class EnemyStats : MonoBehaviour
{
    public bool isInvulnerable;

    // 1. Basic Boolean Inversion
    [HideIf(nameof(isInvulnerable))]
    public int maxHealth = 100;

    // 2. Compound Inline Expression
    [HideIf("$isInvulnerable || $maxHealth <= 0")]
    public float damageVulnerability = 1.0f;
}

Core Framework/Conditional Visibility/[ReadOnlyConditional]

[ReadOnlyConditional]

Conditionally locks a serialized field or property to read-only mode with custom styling based on runtime states, compound C#-style inline expressions, parameterized method validators, or engine state macros.

1. Overview & Value Proposition

What it does: Makes a field read-only (locked from user modification) when a condition evaluates to true, while applying customizable opacity and color tinting to communicate the locked state clearly.

The Problem: Standard [ReadOnly] attributes are static: a field is either permanently locked or permanently editable. In real-world game development, fields often start editable during design setup and must lock down once procedural generation runs, once network synchronization starts, or during runtime Play Mode.

The Solution: Add [ReadOnlyConditional] to your fields:

  • Dynamic Lock State: Switch between editable and locked based on game state, flags, or method return values.
  • Accidental Edit Guard: Protect vital variables (like random seeds or world anchors) from accidental modification during Play Mode using [ReadOnlyConditional("@isPlayMode")].
  • Inline C#-Style Expressions: Lock fields when arbitrary formulas evaluate to true (e.g. [ReadOnlyConditional("$characterHealth <= 0 || $isStunned")]).
  • Parameterized Methods: Re-use a single validator to lock fields based on role or privilege arguments ([ReadOnlyConditional("IsRoleRestricted('Guest')")]).
  • Visual Styling: Fully control locked field opacity (DisabledOpacity = 0.4f) and background hex color tinting (DisabledColor = "#FFA726").
  • Supports Inversion: Pass inverse: true to make the field editable only when the condition is met.

2. Quick Start

csharp
using UnityEngine;
using MaharajaStudio.MSUltimate.Runtime;

public class MatchManager : MonoBehaviour
{
    public bool isMatchLive;

    // 1. Basic Boolean Dynamic Locking
    [ReadOnlyConditional(nameof(isMatchLive))]
    public int maxTeamScore = 50;

    // 2. Play Mode Automatic Lock
    [ReadOnlyConditional("@isPlayMode")]
    public string worldSeedKey = "SEED-PROC-994";
}

Core Framework/Conditional Visibility/[ShowIf]

[ShowIf]

Displays a serialized field, property, or method in the Inspector only when a specified condition evaluates to true.
Supports boolean flags, C#-style compound inline expressions, parameterized method calls, bitwise flags, engine macros, and relative parent traversal.

1. Overview & Value Proposition

What it does: Renders an element in the Inspector only when its condition evaluates to true, collapsing it completely otherwise.

The Problem: Game components frequently have modular settings (e.g., custom weapon configs, audio overrides, AI thresholds, network telemetry) that are only meaningful when specific features or modes are active. In standard Unity, all secondary parameters clutter the Inspector permanently, confusing game designers and cluttering the UI.

The Solution: Add [ShowIf] above your fields, properties, or buttons:

  • Clean Responsive Inspectors: Fields appear only when relevant, drastically reducing cognitive load.
  • Inline C#-Style Expressions: Write compound multi-variable conditions ([ShowIf("$health > 50 && $shield <= 0")]) without writing boilerplate helper properties.
  • Parameterized Methods: Re-use a single validator across multiple fields ([ShowIf("HasPermission('Admin')")]).
  • Bitwise Flag Operations: Test [System.Flags] bitmasks directly using ConditionOperator.HasFlag.
  • Global Engine Macros: Gate settings behind editor states (@isPlayMode, @isEditor, @isPrefabStage, @selectionCount == 1).
  • Parent Traversal: Nested classes can inspect parent settings ([ShowIf("$parent.enableAdvanced")] or [ShowIf("../isUnlocked")]).
  • Zero-Polling Reactivity: Powered by UI Toolkit property tracking for instant 0ms response times.
  • Typo Protection: If a member name is misspelled, MSUltimate logs a suggestion in the console (e.g., "Did you mean 'isAlive'?") rather than failing silently.

2. Quick Start

csharp
using UnityEngine;
using MaharajaStudio.MSUltimate.Runtime;

public class VehicleController : MonoBehaviour
{
    public bool enableTurboBoost;

    // 1. Basic Boolean Toggle

    public float turboSpeedMultiplier = 2.0f;

    // 2. Inline C#-Style Expression (No helper property needed!)
    [ShowIf("$turboSpeedMultiplier >= 3.0 && enableTurboBoost")]
    public ParticleSystem overchargeFlames;
}

using System;
using UnityEngine;
using MaharajaStudio.MSUltimate.Runtime;

public class CombatController : ModularMonoBehaviour
{
    public enum WeaponMode { Melee, Ranged, Magic }

    [Flags]
    public enum ElementAffinities
    {
        None = 0,
        Fire = 1 << 0,
        Frost = 1 << 1,
        Lightning = 1 << 2
    }

    [Serializable]
    public class NestedCombatProfile
    {
        // 1. Sibling / Parent Relative Traversal
        [ShowIf("$parent.enableAdvancedCombat")]
        public float parentDrivenMultiplier = 2.5f;

        [ShowIf("../playerLevel", 20, ConditionOperator.GreaterThanOrEqual)]
        public string masterRankTitle = "Grandmaster";
    }

    [Header("Core State")]
    public bool enableAdvancedCombat = true;
    public WeaponMode activeWeaponMode = WeaponMode.Magic;
    public ElementAffinities activeElements = ElementAffinities.Fire | ElementAffinities.Lightning;
    public int playerLevel = 25;
    public float currentHealth = 20f;
    public bool isInvincible = false;

    // 2. Direct Enum Matching
    [ShowIf(nameof(activeWeaponMode), WeaponMode.Magic)]
    public float manaCostPerCast = 35f;

    // 3. Bitwise Flag Check (HasFlag)
    [ShowIf(nameof(activeElements), ElementAffinities.Fire, ConditionOperator.HasFlag)]
    public float fireBurnDuration = 6.0f;

    // 4. Inline C#-Style Expression (Compound Logic & Precedence)
    [ShowIf("$playerLevel >= 20 && $activeWeaponMode == WeaponMode.Magic")]
    [InfoBox("Archmage Stance Unlocked!", InspectorMessageType.Success)]
    public string ultimateSpell = "Cataclysmic Nova";

    // 5. Expression with Grouping & Negation
    [ShowIf("($currentHealth < 25 || $playerLevel < 5) && !$isInvincible")]
    [InfoBox("Critical Health Warning!", InspectorMessageType.Warning)]
    public Color alertVignetteColor = Color.red;

    // 6. Parameterized Method Invocation
    [ShowIf("CanEquipGear('Excalibur', 20)")]
    public string excaliburGemSocket = "Radiant Diamond";

    // 7. Global Context Engine Macro (@)
    [ShowIf("@isPlayMode")]
    public string liveTelemetry = "Target TPS: 60 | Active Buffs: 3";

    // 8. Nested Object Parent Traversal
    public NestedCombatProfile profile = new NestedCombatProfile();

    // Validator method used by [ShowIf("CanEquipGear(...)")]
    public bool CanEquipGear(string gearName, int minLevel)
    {
        return playerLevel >= minLevel;
    }
}

Core Framework/Specialized Fields/[AngleGauge]

[AngleGauge]

Renders a numeric field or rotation value as an interactive 2D radial dial gauge with angle snapping and compass directions.

1. Overview & Value Proposition

What it does: Renders a visual circular dial or compass gauge with an interactive needle to intuitively rotate angles and directional vectors.

The Problem: Tuning angular bearings, wind directions, or turret firing angles using raw numbers (135.5°, 270°) forces developers to calculate trigonometry in their heads. Designers frequently enter reversed angles or miss quadrant boundaries because numbers alone lack spatial feedback.

The Solution: Add [AngleGauge] to any numeric rotation field:

  • Interactive Radial Needle: Click and drag the gauge needle to rotate angles with immediate visual feedback.
  • Cardinal Compass Markings: Displays North (N), East (E), South (S), and West (W) compass directions.
  • Angle Snapping & Quick Buttons: Snap to customizable increments (e.g. 15°, 45°, 90°) with one-click cardinal preset buttons.
  • Degrees or Radians: Supports both standard Degrees (0–360°) and Radians (0–2π) with clockwise or counter-clockwise orientations.

2. Quick Start

using MaharajaStudio.MSUltimate.Runtime;

public class WindDirector : MonoBehaviour

    [AngleGauge(0, 360, snapAngle: 15f)]
    public float windDirectionDegrees = 45f;

    [AngleGauge(Radians = true, ShowQuickButtons = false)]

Core Framework/Specialized Fields/[AnimatorParam]

[AnimatorParam]

Renders a string or integer hash property as a smart dropdown populated with parameter names from an attached or referenced Animator.

1. Overview & Value Proposition

What it does: Populates a string or integer field with a live dropdown list of animation parameters from your Animator Controller, preventing typos.

The Problem: Triggering animations via animator.SetTrigger("Attack") or animator.SetFloat("Speed", 5f) requires typing magic strings. If an animator renames a parameter in the Animator Controller, the code silently fails with no compile-time error or warning.

The Solution: Add [AnimatorParam] to any string or int parameter field:

  • Live Controller Reflection: Automatically extracts parameters directly from the GameObject's Animator or AnimatorController.
  • Type-Specific Filtering: Filter dropdowns specifically to Trigger, Float, Int, or Bool parameters.
  • Visual Type Badges: Displays colored tags beside parameter names indicating their exact data types.
  • String or Hash Support: Works with both parameter name strings and pre-hashed integer IDs (Animator.StringToHash).

Core Framework/Specialized Fields/[AssetOnly]

[AssetOnly]

Restricts an object reference field to project assets only, preventing scene hierarchy objects from being accidentally assigned.

1. Overview & Value Proposition

What it does: Restricts Object fields to saved Project window assets (prefabs, materials, audio clips, scriptable objects) and rejects scene instances.

The Problem: In ScriptableObjects and prefab assets, dragging a GameObject from the active Scene hierarchy creates an invalid cross-scene reference. When loading another scene or building the game, these scene references break, turning into MissingReferenceException errors.

The Solution: Add [AssetOnly] to any object reference field:

  • Scene Reference Block: Disallows dragging or selecting objects from the active scene hierarchy.
  • Immediate Warning Callout: Displays an informative warning box when an invalid scene object is dragged into the field.
  • Auto-Clear Protection: Enable AutoClear = true to automatically reject and wipe invalid scene assignments.
  • Collection Support: Fully validated inside lists, arrays, and serialized dictionaries of assets.

2. Quick Start

csharp
using UnityEngine;
using MaharajaStudio.MSUltimate.Runtime;

[CreateAssetMenu(menuName = "Game/Weapon Config")]
public class WeaponConfig : ScriptableObject
{
    [AssetOnly]
    public GameObject weaponPrefab;

    [AssetOnly(AutoClear = true)]
    public AudioClip fireSfx;
}

[AutoFill]

Automatically searches and assigns matching Component references in the Inspector across Self, Children, Parent, or Scene scopes.

1. Overview & Value Proposition

What it does: Auto-detects and connects missing Component references (like Rigidbody, AudioSource, or Collider) the moment an object is inspected or initialized.

The Problem: Connecting boilerplate component references by dragging and dropping them into serialized fields on every GameObject is tedious and error-prone. Forgetting to drag a Rigidbody or Animator causes frustrating NullReferenceException crashes when running play mode.

The Solution: Add [AutoFill] to any Component field:

  • Flexible Search Scopes: Search Self, Children, Parent, or the active Scene automatically.
  • Tag Filtering: Scope scene-wide searches to objects with specific tags (e.g. "Player" or "GameController").
  • Auto-Filled Badge: Renders a clean pill badge indicating that the component was automatically resolved.
  • Overwrite Protection: By default, preserves manually assigned references unless Overwrite = true is set.

Core Framework/Specialized Fields/[AutoRename]

[AutoRename]

Automatically renames referenced scene GameObjects or components to match clean naming patterns, eliminating generic Unity default names (GameObject (1), (Clone)) in the hierarchy with automatic and button-controlled manual modes.

1. Overview & Value Proposition

What it does: Automatically renames referenced GameObjects or Components assigned in the Inspector to match a clean, customizable naming pattern (e.g. {FieldName}, {Host}_{FieldName}, or {FieldName}_{Index:00}). Includes an inline button for on-demand manual renaming, supports automatic (Clone) suffix stripping, and handles sibling collision deduplication.

The Problem: In standard Unity development, creating new game objects or instantiating prefabs results in generic default names like GameObject (1), GameObject (2), or EnemyVariantA(Clone). When these objects are assigned to fields on other components, it is difficult to determine which object is referenced without clicking each field to ping the hierarchy. Over time, scene hierarchies become messy and confusing.

The Solution: Add [AutoRename] above any object reference field or collection:

  • Clean Hierarchy Hygiene: Automatically converts generic names into descriptive, context-aware names matching their field role.
  • Both Auto and Manual Modes: Choose between automatic renaming on assignment (AutoRenameMode.Auto) or intentional button-driven renaming (AutoRenameMode.Manual).
  • Inline Action Button: Render an ergonomic button beside the field control (styled like [SetRandomValue]) to trigger or re-run renaming at any time.
  • Dynamic Token Formatting: Construct names using tokens like {FieldName}, {Host}, {Component}, {Type}, {Original}, and {Index:00}.
  • Designer Name Protection: With RenameCondition.OnlyIfDefault (the default), existing custom-named objects are preserved and never overwritten by accident.
  • Prefab Asset Safety: By default, restricts renaming strictly to scene instances (SceneObjectsOnly = true), preventing accidental modification of project prefab files on disk.

2. Quick Start

csharp
using UnityEngine;
using MaharajaStudio.MSUltimate.Runtime;

public class PlayerCombatRig : MonoBehaviour
{
    // Dragging "GameObject (1)" automatically renames it to "MuzzlePoint"
    [AutoRename]
    public Transform muzzlePoint;

    // Names using host context: "Player_CombatRig_CameraPivot"
    [AutoRename("{Host}_{FieldName}")]
    public Transform cameraPivot;
}

[Calendar]

The Problem: Entering dates and timestamps in Unity requires typing arbitrary date strings (like "2026-10-15 14:30:00") or calculating Unix epoch seconds by hand. A single formatting error, missing zero, or invalid day causes silent serialization bugs and live-ops parsing crashes.

  • Rich Theme Presets: Choose from built-in theme presets (Ocean, Emerald, Midnight, Sunset, Violet) or custom colors.
  • Multi-Format Storage: Works on string, long (Ticks, Unix seconds/milliseconds), int, and SerializableDateTime.

Core Framework/Specialized Fields/[CustomRange]

[CustomRange]

Renders a numeric field as an enhanced slider with custom limits, dynamic member bounds, step snapping, and styling.

1. Overview & Value Proposition

What it does: Upgrades standard numeric range sliders with step snapping, dynamic min/max bounds, decimal precision, and custom colors.

The Problem: Unity's built-in [Range] attribute is static: min and max values must be compile-time constants. You cannot bind limits dynamically to another property (like maxAmmo), cannot snap slider dragging to discrete steps (like 0.25), and cannot style track colors.

The Solution: Add [CustomRange] to any numeric field:

  • Dynamic Min/Max Limits: Bind limits dynamically to float/int member fields or methods (e.g. minLevel, maxLevel).
  • Step Snapping: Snap values to exact increments (e.g. Step = 0.5f or Step = 5f).
  • Decimal Precision Control: Enforce exact decimal rounding (e.g. Decimals = 2).
  • Integrated Number Box: Displays an editable numeric field alongside the slider track.

2. Quick Start

csharp
using UnityEngine;
using MaharajaStudio.MSUltimate.Runtime;

public class WeaponStats : MonoBehaviour
{
    [CustomRange(0f, 100f)]
    public float damage = 25f;

    [CustomRange(0f, 10f, Step = 0.25f)]
    public float reloadTime = 2.5f;
}

Core Framework/Specialized Fields/[DecibelVolume]

[DecibelVolume]

Transforms a volume field into a logarithmic Audio Decibel (dB) slider with a VU meter, mute toggle, and linear readouts.

1. Overview & Value Proposition

What it does: Converts standard linear volume floats into a professional audio mixer slider measured in Decibels (dB) with a live VU meter and mute toggle.

The Problem: Human hearing perceives loudness logarithmically, not linearly. Setting volumes with simple 0.0 to 1.0 sliders makes subtle adjustments at lower volumes impossible and requires tedious manual 20 * log10(volume) calculations when interfacing with Unity's AudioMixer.

The Solution: Add [DecibelVolume] to any audio volume field:

  • True Logarithmic Audio Slider: Scales naturally from silence (-80 dB) up to unity gain (0 dB) and boosted gain (+6 dB).
  • Visual LED / VU Level Meter: Renders an authentic multi-colored audio level meter bar beside the slider.
  • One-Click Mute Speaker: Quickly mute and unmute audio channels during play testing.
  • Dual Serialization Modes: Store as standard Linear amplitude (0.0-1.0) or directly as raw Decibels for AudioMixer.SetFloat.
