Core Framework/Specialized Fields/[Delayed]

[Delayed]

Defers updating the serialized property until the user presses Enter or the input field loses focus.

1. Overview & Value Proposition

What it does: Prevents immediate property value updates on every single keystroke, committing the value only when you press Enter or click away.

The Problem: In standard Unity, typing a number or string updates the serialized property on every typed character. If a setter or OnValidate method re-generates meshes, recalculates pathfinding, or triggers web requests, typing "1000" will run expensive rebuilds 4 times (1, 10, 100, 1000), freezing the editor.

The Solution: Add [Delayed] to any text or numeric field:

  • Batch Expensive Rebuilds: Commit changes only when the user finishes typing and presses Enter or un-focuses the field.
  • Prevents Intermediate Invalids: Avoids temporary zero or single-digit values from triggering validation errors while typing.
  • Broad Data Type Support: Supported on float, int, string, double, and long.
  • Zero Runtime Overhead: Operates strictly within the UI Toolkit field change event pipeline.

2. Quick Start

csharp
using UnityEngine;
using MaharajaStudio.MSUltimate.Runtime;

public class TerrainBakeSettings : MonoBehaviour
{
    [Delayed]
    public int voxelResolution = 512;

    [Delayed]
    public string remoteApiEndpoint = "https://api.game.internal/v1/config";
}

        [InfoBox("[Delayed] implements ICollectionElementAttribute to cascade delayed commit input fields down into raw arrays and lists automatically.", InspectorMessageType.Info)]

        [Delayed]
        public float[] physicsSubstepScales = new float[] { 0.016f, 0.008f, 0.004f };

        [ButtonGroup("DelayedActions")]
        [Button("Print Committed Server Config", BackgroundColor = "#0284C7", TextColor = "#FFFFFF")]
        private void PrintServerConfig()
        {
            Debug.Log($"[Delayed] Primary: {primaryServer.serverHost}:{primaryServer.listenPort} | Scale: {renderScale}");
        }
    }

Core Framework/Specialized Fields/[GrabFromChild]

[GrabFromChild]

Intercepts drag-and-drop operations on object reference and collection fields, allowing developers to drop any ancestor or parent GameObject to automatically resolve, extract, and assign nested child components.

1. Overview & Value Proposition

What it does: [GrabFromChild] solves one of the most frustrating bottlenecks in Unity game development: assigning references to components or bones buried 10–20 levels deep in a GameObject hierarchy. Instead of forcing you to expand endless hierarchy folds to find a nested child, you can drop any visible parent or root GameObject directly onto the field—[GrabFromChild] searches the hierarchy, extracts the matching component, and assigns it instantly.

The Problem:

  • Standard Unity ObjectField is strictly type-bound: if your field is Hitbox, dragging Character_Root is immediately rejected with a "not allowed" cursor.
  • Manually expanding skeletal armatures (Root/Pelvis/Spine/Chest/Shoulder/Arm/Hand/WeaponSocket) is tedious, slow, and collapses if the Inspector accidentally loses focus.
  • Populating collections (e.g. List<Collider> or List<ParticleSystem>) requires dragging dozens of child objects one-by-one.

The Solution:

  • Zero Hierarchy Diving: Drop Character_Root directly into headBone, weaponSocket, or characterHitboxes.
  • Search Modes & Depth: Choose between Recursive (all descendants), DirectChildren (immediate only), SelfThenRecursive, or SelfThenDirect.
  • Name & Wildcard Filtering: Scope searches using patterns like "Head", "*Socket*", or "Muzzle*".
  • Disambiguation Modes: Automatically picks the FirstMatch, LastMatch, or opens an interactive PromptIfMultiple popup menu if several matches exist.
  • Bulk Collection Auto-Fill: Drop a parent into a List<T> or T[] to populate all matching child components in a single click (Replace or Append).
  • Clean Field Integration: Retains 100% of standard Unity inspector styling with zero UI clutter or extra buttons.

2. Quick Start

csharp
using UnityEngine;
using MaharajaStudio.MSUltimate.Runtime;

public class CharacterRigBindings : MonoBehaviour
{
    // Drop Character_Root here -> automatically finds the child bone containing "Head"
    [GrabFromChild("Head")]
    public Transform headBone;

    // Drop Weapon_Prefab here -> automatically finds and assigns the audio source
    [GrabFromChild]
    public AudioSource weaponAudio;

    // Drop Character_Root here -> fills all child colliders into the list in bulk
    [GrabFromChild]
    public List<BoxCollider> hitboxes = new List<BoxCollider>();
}

Core Framework/Specialized Fields/[Hide]

[Hide]

Completely hides a serialized field or property from being drawn in the Inspector.

1. Overview & Value Proposition

What it does: Conceals a public or [SerializeField] variable entirely from the Inspector without breaking its serialization or network replication.

The Problem: Variables often need to be public (for other scripts to access) or serialized (so Unity saves their values in scenes, prefabs, or network packets). However, displaying internal cache IDs or runtime-managed data in the Inspector confuses designers and risks accidental manual tampering.

The Solution: Add [Hide] to any serialized field:

  • Preserves Full Serialization: Unity continues to serialize and save the field value without rendering it.
  • Leaves Public APIs Intact: Keep fields public for high-performance direct script access without Inspector exposure.
  • Replaces [HideInInspector]: Fully integrated into MSUltimate's UI Toolkit layout and grouping pipeline.
  • Zero Overhead: Completely skipped during VisualElement generation passes.

2. Quick Start

csharp
using UnityEngine;
using MaharajaStudio.MSUltimate.Runtime;

public class NetworkEntity : MonoBehaviour
{

Core Framework/Specialized Fields/[LinkedField]

[LinkedField]

Couples two numeric inspector fields with an interactive chain toggle to synchronize values proportionally, additively, or as inverse/exact mirrors.

1. Overview & Value Proposition

What it does: Binds two numeric serialized fields together (such as width & height, minimum & maximum, or speed & acceleration) via an interactive chain link icon in the Inspector. When linked, editing one field automatically updates the other according to the selected mathematical mode.

The Problem: In game development, many numeric values are intrinsically coupled—such as UI element dimensions, camera frustum ratios, bounding box extents, or audio pitch/reverb relationships. In default Unity, developers must manually calculate and enter reciprocal values or write custom OnValidate boilerplate for every pair of properties.

The Solution: Applying [LinkedField] provides:

  • Interactive Chain Toggle: A clickable chain icon right beside the field allows designers to toggle synchronization on or off at runtime or in edit mode.
  • Multiple Mathematical Modes:
    • LinkMode.Proportional: Multiplies by the initial ratio (e.g. maintaining 16:9 aspect ratios when resizing resolution).
    • LinkMode.Additive: Preserves the fixed numerical difference/offset between both values.
    • LinkMode.Mirror: Clones the exact value across both fields simultaneously.
  • Bi-Directional Synchronization: Changing either field updates its linked partner smoothly without infinite loop recursions.

2. Quick Start

csharp
using UnityEngine;
using MaharajaStudio.MSUltimate.Runtime;

public class TextureResolutionConfig : MonoBehaviour
{
    public int textureWidth = 1920;

    [LinkedField("textureWidth", LinkMode.Proportional, startLinked: true)]
    public int textureHeight = 1080;
}

Core Framework/Specialized Fields/[ManageableAsset]

[ManageableAsset]

Registers ScriptableObject classes directly into the MSUltimate Asset Manager Window for centralized cataloging, filtering, and 1-click instantiation.

1. Overview & Value Proposition

What it does: Decorates a ScriptableObject class to register it as an indexed asset catalog entry in the MSUltimate Asset Manager. Once tagged, designers and programmers can browse, filter, inspect, and instantiate instances of this asset type through a single unified project-wide manager window.

The Problem: In mid-to-large Unity projects, ScriptableObjects become scattered across deeply nested folders (Assets/GameData/Items/Weapons/...). Locating existing data assets requires tedious navigation in the Project window, and remembering their [CreateAssetMenu] path causes friction for team members creating new balance configs or quest definitions.

The Solution: Add [ManageableAsset] to any ScriptableObject class definition:

  • Centralized Hub: Automatically gathers all project instances of this ScriptableObject into the Asset Manager Window (Tools > Maharaja Studio > MSUltimate > Windows > Asset Manager).
  • Categorized Menu Tree: Groups types hierarchically (e.g. "Inventory/Weapons", "Dialogue/Quests").
  • 1-Click Creation & Renaming: Fast creation with predefined template names and folder targets without right-clicking menus.
  • Visual Branding: Custom icons and descriptions display directly in the Asset Manager registry.

Locks fields, properties, or buttons against user edits in the Inspector while keeping them visible, with optional dynamic conditional rules.

What it does: Disables interaction for decorated serialized fields, properties, or inspector buttons so they cannot be modified by designers, while remaining visible for debugging and telemetry. Supports dynamic condition members to toggle read-only state on the fly.

The Problem: Developers frequently need to display internal state—such as current health, calculated DPS, unique entity GUIDs, or weapon cooldown states—in the Inspector so team members can monitor them during testing. Without a read-only attribute, designers might inadvertently change calculated fields or break system identifiers during runtime.

The Solution: Add [ReadOnly] to any target:

  • Unconditional Locking: Simply mark [ReadOnly] to keep the field permanently grayed out and unmodifiable.
  • Dynamic Condition Binding: Pass a boolean field, property, or method name to toggle read-only state conditionally (e.g. [ReadOnly("isLockedInCombat")]).
  • Inverse Evaluation: Pass inverse: true to make the field read-only when the condition evaluates to false.
  • Custom Visual Styling: Adjust DisabledOpacity or inject custom disabled text colors to tailor visual hierarchy.

Core Framework/Specialized Fields/[SceneObjectOnly]

[SceneObjectOnly]

Restricts object reference fields strictly to active Scene hierarchy instances, blocking project assets and prefabs from invalid assignment.

1. Overview & Value Proposition

What it does: Enforces that an object reference field (e.g. Transform, GameObject, Collider) can only be populated by objects existing in the active scene hierarchy. If a designer drags a project asset or prefab asset from the Project browser, it immediately flags a warning or auto-rejects the assignment.

The Problem: Certain gameplay references—such as patrol waypoints, player spawn points, cinematic cameras, or room boundary triggers—must exist as physical scene instances in the level. Accidentally dragging an uninstantiated prefab asset into a scene-only reference causes silent runtime bugs, broken positions, or missing component errors.

The Solution: Add [SceneObjectOnly] to any UnityEngine.Object field:

  • Instant Drag Validation: Detects whether an assigned asset resides in the Project database or an instantiated scene.
  • Configurable Auto-Clear: Automatically nullifies illegal project asset assignments if AutoClear = true.
  • Active Scene Restriction: Restricts references strictly to the currently active scene in multi-scene editing setups (RequireInActiveScene = true).
  • Customizable Warning Banners: Formats clear warning messages with custom text and styling.

2. Quick Start

csharp
using UnityEngine;
using MaharajaStudio.MSUltimate.Runtime;

public class PatrolAgent : MonoBehaviour
{
    [SceneObjectOnly]
    public Transform patrolRouteAnchor;
}

Core Framework/Specialized Fields/[SceneQuery]

[SceneQuery]

Renders string scene path/name fields as a searchable dropdown populated from project scenes with 1-click ping and Build Settings validation.

1. Overview & Value Proposition

What it does: Populates a string field with an interactive dropdown list of scenes from the active Unity Project or Build Settings. Includes automatic detection of missing build scenes, an inline "Ping" button to highlight the Scene asset in the Project browser, and path filtering.

The Problem: Loading scenes in Unity using strings (like SceneManager.LoadScene("Level_02")) is error-prone. A typo in the level name causes fatal loading failures in standalone builds. Additionally, if a level has not been added to Build Settings, developers are only alerted when the build fails or throws exceptions at runtime.

The Solution: Add [SceneQuery] to any string field:

  • Drop-Down Scene Picker: Choose scenes directly from a clean dropdown instead of manually typing scene names.
  • Build Settings Validation: Warns immediately in the Inspector if the selected scene is missing from Unity's Build Settings (DisplayWarningIfMissing = true).
  • Ping Asset Button: Instantly locate and ping the .unity scene asset in the Project view with a single click.
  • Path & Filtering Options: Filter scenes by name patterns, toggle between simple scene names or full asset paths, and query either Build scenes or all project scenes.

Core Framework/Specialized Fields/[SetNextValue]

[SetNextValue]

Automatically assigns sequential numbers, auto-incremented counters, or collection index formulas upon creation, with an inline step button (⏭).

1. Overview & Value Proposition

What it does: Automatically seeds sequential, incremental, or list-index-driven numbers and formatted string codes when a new component is added, an asset is created, or a new item is inserted into a List/Array. Includes an inline ⏭ step button right in the Inspector to advance to the next value at any time.

The Problem: Creating lists of sequential game data—such as quest IDs ("Quest_001", "Quest_002"), dialogue line numbers, inventory slot identifiers, or audio channel indexes—requires tedious manual entry. Designers frequently make typos or duplicate IDs, leading to corrupted save files and progression bugs.

The Solution: Add [SetNextValue] to numeric or string fields:

  • Automatic Auto-Increment: New list items or components automatically receive the next counter value (StartValue + Step).
  • Formatted Strings: Formats integers into strings with custom prefixes, suffixes, and padding (e.g. Prefix = "Quest_", Format = "D3" produces "Quest_001", "Quest_002").
  • Collection Index Binding: When placed inside a List or Array, automatically mirrors element indices via (Index * Step + StartValue).
  • Custom Source Members: Pulls sequential values from a custom generator method or cycles through a predefined array.
  • Manual Step Button: Click the inline ⏭ button to increment to the next sequence value on demand.

2. Quick Start

using UnityEngine;
using MaharajaStudio.MSUltimate.Runtime;

    public string questIdentifier = "Quest_001";

    [SetNextValue(10, step: 5)]
    public int baseExpReward = 10;
}

Core Framework/Specialized Fields/[SortingLayerSelector]

[SortingLayerSelector]

Displays integer (Layer ID) or string (Layer Name) fields as a native Unity 2D Sorting Layer dropdown with 1-click Project Settings access.

1. Overview & Value Proposition

What it does: Transforms standard int (Sorting Layer ID) or string (Sorting Layer Name) fields into an interactive dropdown menu populated directly with the project's 2D Sorting Layers. Includes an inline gear button to jump straight to Unity's Tags & Layers project settings.

The Problem: In 2D projects, custom components (like custom mesh generators, VFX emitters, or custom sprite controllers) often need to specify a sorting layer. Without a drawer, developers must remember exact string names (e.g. "Foreground", "Characters") or raw integer IDs, leading to typos and layer ordering bugs that render sprites behind the background.

The Solution: Add [SortingLayerSelector] to int, uint, or string fields:

  • Automatic Layer Discovery: Fetches the exact sorting layers configured in the project in real time.
  • Dual Representation Support: Works seamlessly with string fields (serializing layer names like "Default") or int fields (serializing unique layer IDs).
  • 1-Click Tags & Layers Shortcut: Click the gear icon to immediately open Project Settings → Tags & Layers.
  • Visual Customization: Supports custom label overrides, text colors, and background styling.

Core Framework/Specialized Fields/[TypeFilter]

[TypeFilter]

Restricts object reference fields to GameObjects or Components that implement a specific interface or inherit from an abstract base class.

1. Overview & Value Proposition

What it does: Enforces type constraints on serialized object fields (such as MonoBehaviour, Component, or UnityEngine.Object), restricting drag-and-drop assignment strictly to assets or components that implement a specified C# interface or inherit from a specific abstract class.

The Problem: Unity cannot serialize interface types directly (e.g. public IDamageable target; does not appear in the Inspector). To work around this, developers serialize MonoBehaviour or GameObject references and cast them in Awake(). However, designers can accidentally drag any unrelated component into the field, causing NullReferenceException or InvalidCastException crashes when playing.

The Solution: Add [TypeFilter(typeof(IInterface))] to your serialized field:

  • Interface Drag Validation: Object picker popup and drag-and-drop operations only accept components implementing the target interface.
  • Visual Feedback: Objects lacking the expected interface or base type are immediately rejected or highlighted with an error banner.
  • Abstract Base Class Filtering: Restrict assignments to specific subclass branches.
  • Collection Support: Full support for List<MonoBehaviour> or interface collections via ICollectionElementAttribute.

2. Quick Start

csharp
using UnityEngine;
using MaharajaStudio.MSUltimate.Runtime;

public interface IDamageable
{
    void TakeDamage(float amount);
}

public class AttackTrigger : MonoBehaviour
{
    [TypeFilter(typeof(IDamageable))]
    public MonoBehaviour damageTarget;
}

[UnitConverter]

Displays live converted physical units (meters to feet, km/h to mph, Celsius to Fahrenheit) inside a sleek badge beside numeric fields.

However, many designers, artists, and international team members think in imperial units (feet, miles, pounds, degrees, Fahrenheit). The Solution: Add [UnitConverter] to any numeric field:

What it does: Transforms standard serialized fields (strings, ints, floats, objects, or structs) into a rich dropdown menu populated dynamically from a C# method, property, or collection member that returns an IEnumerable. Supports custom display labels via ValueDropdownList<T>.

The Problem: Game configuration often depends on data created elsewhere in code—such as audio bus names loaded from an audio manager, spawn node identifiers declared across a scene, or items queried from a database. The Solution: Add [ValueDropdown("MyValuesGetter")] to any field:

  • Dynamic Member Sourcing: Pulls options directly from methods, properties, or fields returning IEnumerable, arrays, or lists.
  • Label-Value Decoupling: Use ValueDropdownList<T> to display friendly designer labels ("Sword of Destiny (Tier 5)") while storing exact underlying values ("item_swd_005").
  • Alphabetical Sorting: Toggle automatic alphabetical sorting via SortItems = true.
  • Optional Empty State: Enable AllowEmpty = true to provide a default (None) option.

Core Framework/Buttons & Actions/[Button]

[Button]

Renders an interactive, styled execution button in the Inspector that invokes C# methods with custom icons, colors, parameter input panels, and layout sizing.

1. Overview & Value Proposition

What it does: Turns any regular C# method into a clickable, styled button right in the Unity Inspector.

The Problem: In standard Unity, there is no built-in way to test or run a method from the Inspector. To test spawning an enemy, resetting a save file, or executing a custom action, you have to write a custom Editor script, create right-click context menus, or enter Play Mode and trigger it with keyboard shortcuts.

The Solution: Add [Button] above any method, field, or property. It instantly generates a clean, interactive button:

  • 1-Click Execution: Run methods directly in Edit Mode or Play Mode with a single click.
  • Custom Styling: Change button text, background colors, text colors, icons, and button height to make key actions stand out.
  • Parameter Support: Supports methods with parameters, providing an expandable parameters panel and settings foldout.
  • Conditional Visibility & Interactivity: Built-in ShowIf and EnableIf properties for dynamic reactivity.

2. Quick Start

csharp
using UnityEngine;
using MaharajaStudio.MSUltimate.Runtime;

public class Spawner : MonoBehaviour
{
    [Button("Spawn Wave", colorHex: "#27AE60")]
    public void TriggerSpawn()
    {
        Debug.Log("Spawning wave of enemies!");
    }
}

7. Stacking & Compatibility Matrix

  • Grouping: Pairs seamlessly inside [BoxGroup], [HorizontalGroup], and [CardGroup]. Inside horizontal groups, multiple buttons arrange side-by-side into sleek action toolbars.
  • Conditionals: Respects ShowIf and EnableIf properties directly without needing external wrapper attributes.
  • Undo Integration: Modifications triggered by the method are registered in Unity's Undo stack when modifying serialized properties.
Core Framework/Buttons & Actions/[CopyPaste]

[CopyPaste]

Attaches compact "Copy" and "Paste" action buttons adjacent to serialized fields and complex structs for instant data transfer.

1. Overview & Value Proposition

What it does: Adds dedicated "Copy" and "Paste" buttons next to any field or struct for instant data transfer.

The Problem: Copying complex settings (like character stats, animation curves, color palettes, or arrays) between GameObjects in standard Unity is tedious. You either have to copy the whole component and overwrite everything else, or manually re-type every number one by one.

The Solution: Add [CopyPaste] above any field, struct, or class:

  • 1-Click Clipboard: Click "Copy" to save data to the system clipboard, and "Paste" to apply it to any matching field.
  • Works on Complex Structs: Copies entire classes, nested data structures, arrays, and lists seamlessly.
  • Cross-Scene & Prefab Transfer: Easily transfer data across different GameObjects, prefabs, or even across different scenes.
  • Full Undo Support: Every paste operation registers with Unity's Undo system (Ctrl+Z), so your work is always safe.

2. Quick Start

csharp
using System;
using UnityEngine;
using MaharajaStudio.MSUltimate.Runtime;

public class CharacterPreset : MonoBehaviour
{
    [Serializable]
    public struct CombatStats
    {
        public float baseAttack;
        public float defense;
        public float criticalChance;
    }

    [CopyPaste]
    public CombatStats stats;
}

Core Framework/Buttons & Actions/[IconButton]

[IconButton]

Injects a compact, inline icon button directly beside a serialized field to trigger utility actions with confirmation dialogs and tooltip hints.

1. Overview & Value Proposition

What it does: Places a compact, inline icon button right next to any field to trigger helper actions without taking up vertical space.

The Problem: Standard buttons take up a full row in the Inspector. When an action is directly tied to a specific field (like "Ping Asset", "Reset to Default", or "Focus Camera on Target"), a full-width button wastes valuable screen space and clutters the UI.

The Solution: Add [IconButton] next to any field:

  • Zero Vertical Waste: Docks neatly at the end of the field's row, keeping your Inspector compact.
  • Unity Built-in Icons: Supports any built-in Unity Editor icon name (e.g. d_ViewToolOrbit, Refresh, d_Search Icon).
  • Hover Tooltips: Shows helpful tooltip hints when designers hover over the icon.
  • Safe Execution: Optional confirmation prompt before triggering sensitive method calls.

2. Quick Start

csharp
using UnityEngine;
using MaharajaStudio.MSUltimate.Runtime;

public class TargetLocator : MonoBehaviour
{
    [IconButton("d_ViewToolOrbit", nameof(FocusTarget), tooltip: "Frame target in SceneView")]
    public Transform targetTransform;

    private void FocusTarget()
    {
        if (targetTransform != null)
            Debug.Log($"Focusing on {targetTransform.name}");
    }
}

        public class PatrolWaypointNode
        {
            public string waypointName = "Alpha_Point";

            [IconButton("d_MoveTool", nameof(SnapToTerrain), "Snap waypoint to terrain surface height", ButtonColor = "#3B82F6")]
            public Vector3 worldPosition = new Vector3(0, 0, 0);

        // ─── 3. Direct Collections Cascading Showcase ────────────────────────────

        [InfoBox("[IconButton] implements ICollectionElementAttribute to automatically add compact icon buttons to individual rows in arrays and lists without wrapper classes.", InspectorMessageType.Info)]

        [IconButton("d_MoveTool", nameof(SnapWaypointIndex), "Snap this waypoint to ground elevation", ButtonColor = "#3B82F6")]
        public Vector3[] perimeterPatrolPoints = new Vector3[]
        {
            new Vector3(0, 4.5f, 0),
            new Vector3(15, 2.8f, -10),
            new Vector3(30, 8.1f, 15)
        };

        [IconButton("d_Refresh", nameof(PingEndpoint), "Ping and re-validate this server cluster node", ButtonColor = "#10B981")]
        public List<string> clusterEndpoints = new List<string>
        {
            "https://cluster-us-east.net",
            "https://cluster-eu-central.net"
        };

        // ─── 4. Interactive Playground Actions ───────────────────────────────────
        [BoxGroup("4. Interactive Playground", BackgroundColor = "#0F172A", BorderColor = "#EAB308", BorderRadius = 6)]
        [Button("Simulate Patrol Route Execution", BackgroundColor = "#10B981", TextColor = "#FFFFFF")]
        public void SimulatePatrolExecution()
        {
            Debug.Log($"[IconButton] Patrol route initialized with {perimeterPatrolPoints.Length} waypoints.");
        }

        private void RandomizePosition() => spawnPosition = UnityEngine.Random.insideUnitSphere * 10f;
        private void ResetAllData() => playerProfile = "Default_Player";
        private void SnapWaypointIndex() { for (int i = 0; i < perimeterPatrolPoints.Length; i++) perimeterPatrolPoints[i].y = 0f; }
        private void PingEndpoint() => Debug.Log("[IconButton] Pinged cluster nodes.");
    }
}

Core Framework/Buttons & Actions/[KeyPad]

[KeyPad]

Transforms string, integer, and float fields into an interactive, visual on-screen keypad or keyboard with tactile themes and custom keymaps.

1. Overview & Value Proposition

What it does: Adds a clickable on-screen keypad (like a numpad or calculator) directly below numeric or text fields.

The Problem: Typing puzzle codes, safe passcodes, PIN numbers, or calculator inputs into generic text boxes doesn't feel like building a game. It is slow for quick testing and makes door/security systems hard to preview the way a player would experience them.

The Solution: Add [KeyPad] above any string, int, or float field or property:

  • Tactile On-Screen Input: Tap numbers and letters using an interactive visual keypad right in the Inspector.
  • Multiple Layouts: Choose between Numpad, Calculator, Phone, Qwerty, and Custom layouts with one setting.
  • Visual Themes: Switch styles between Default, Dark, Light, Neumorphism, and retro Hacker themes.
  • Custom Keypads: Define custom grids of rows and keys with simple pipe and comma notation ("1,2,3|4,5,6|7,8,9|C,0,OK").
  • Optional Digital Display Screen: Display an LCD-style digital value readout above the keypad.

2. Quick Start

csharp
using UnityEngine;
using MaharajaStudio.MSUltimate.Runtime;

public class SecurityDoor : MonoBehaviour
{
    [KeyPad(KeyPadLayout.Numpad, Theme = KeyPadTheme.Dark)]
    public string doorPasscode = "1234";
}

Core Framework/Buttons & Actions/[RandomSeedGenerator]

[RandomSeedGenerator]

Attaches a 1-click randomize dice button and seed history tracker beside integer seed fields for procedural generation workflows.

1. Overview & Value Proposition

What it does: Adds a 1-click randomize button (dice icon) and recent seed history chips next to integer seed fields.

The Problem: Testing procedural worlds, dungeon layouts, or random loot requires changing seeds constantly. In standard Unity, you have to manually click the field, backspace, and mash random numbers on your keyboard over and over again. Plus, if you find a seed you liked, it's easy to accidentally overwrite and lose it forever.

The Solution: Add [RandomSeedGenerator] to any int, uint, or long seed field:

  • 1-Click Randomize: Hit the dice button to instantly generate a new random seed.
  • Seed History Chips: Keeps track of recently generated seeds so you can jump back to a great world layout anytime.
  • Customizable Random Source: Choose between UnityEngine.Random and System.Random.
  • Fast Procedural Iteration: Speeds up testing for terrain, noise generation, and roguelike level generators.

2. Quick Start

csharp
using UnityEngine;
using MaharajaStudio.MSUltimate.Runtime;

public class TerrainGenerator : MonoBehaviour
{
    [RandomSeedGenerator]
    public int worldSeed = 1337;
}

1. Overview & Value Proposition

The Problem: Unity's default 14-pixel checkboxes are tiny, easy to miss, and lack visual punch. For important settings (like "God Mode", "Mute Audio", or "AI Active"), a small checkmark doesn't give you the quick visual confirmation you need when testing.

The Solution: Add [ToolbarToggle] to any bool or enum field:

  • Big, Clickable Push-Buttons: Turns checkboxes into sleek, satisfying toolbar toggle buttons.
  • Custom Colors & Icons: Give active and inactive states distinct background colors, borders, and icons.
  • Custom Labels: Rename options to clear terms like "ACTIVE / DISABLED" or "MUTED / UNMUTED".
  • Enum Support: Expands enums into a horizontal segmented toolbar where you can see and click every option directly.

The Problem: When storing web links in string fields (like documentation links, API URLs, bug tracker pages, or Discord server links), opening them in standard Unity requires manually selecting the text, copying it, opening your browser, and pasting the URL. The Solution: Add [UrlField] above any string containing a website link:

  • 1-Click Web Launch: Click the button beside the field to launch the web page immediately.

  • Link Validation: Automatically verifies the URL format and warns you if the link is malformed or invalid.

Core Framework/Collections/[BaseCollection]

[BaseCollection]

Base configuration attribute for MSUltimate advanced collection and dictionary drawers providing pagination, real-time search, clipboard tools, and custom themes.

1. Overview & Value Proposition

What it does: Provides advanced search, pagination, copy/paste, and visual styling options for lists, arrays, and custom collections.

The Problem: Unity's default ReorderableList is basic and clunky. Once a list grows beyond 20 items, the Inspector scrolls forever, lag spikes occur during repaint, there is no way to search for specific items, and copying entries between lists is impossible.

The Solution: Add collection styling attributes inherited from [BaseCollection]:

  • Instant Search Bar: Filter lists with hundreds of elements instantly by typing keywords.
  • Smart Pagination: Break massive lists into clean pages (e.g. 10 or 15 items per page) to eliminate Inspector scroll lag.
  • Clipboard & Batch Operations: 1-click copy/paste array items, clear collections, or duplicate entries with full Undo support.
  • Custom Visual Styling: Set alternating row colors, rounded borders, custom header banners, and empty placeholder labels.

Customizes the visual presentation of SerializableDateTime fields with quick-set buttons for Now, Today, and Clear, plus configurable Date/Time section visibility.

1. Overview & Value Proposition

What it does: Transforms complex date and time fields (SerializableDateTime) into a polished, user-friendly editor interface. Adds one-click quick-set action buttons ("Now", "Today", "Clear") and allows toggling date or time components on and off.

The Problem: Entering dates, event timestamps, savefile creation times, or seasonal event windows in the Unity Inspector often requires manually entering year, month, day, hour, minute, and second values across multiple numeric fields, which is slow and error-prone.

The Solution: Decorate any SerializableDateTime field with [DrawDateTime]:

  • Quick-Action Buttons: Instantly stamp the current system time ("Now") or today's midnight timestamp ("Today").
  • Flexible Section Filtering: Use HideTime = true for date-only calendars (e.g. daily rewards) or HideDate = true for time-of-day clocks.
  • Reset Support: Fast one-click "Clear" button resets timestamps to zero/epoch.

Core Framework/Core Validation/[ClampWarning]

[ClampWarning]

Displays a non-intrusive warning box when a numeric value falls outside a recommended soft range without hard clamping.

1. Overview & Value Proposition

What it does: Monitors numeric fields (float, int, double, etc.) against a recommended "soft" boundary range. If the value falls below SoftMin or exceeds SoftMax, it renders a styled non-intrusive warning banner directly beneath the field in the Inspector without forcibly clamping or reverting the user's input.

The Problem: Hard limits ([Range], Mathf.Clamp) prevent designers from testing edge-case values or extreme tuning outside typical limits. Conversely, having no feedback allows accidental out-of-spec values that cause physics explosions or performance degradation.

The Solution: Add [ClampWarning] to numeric fields:

  • Soft Guidance: Warns developers when values are outside recommended ranges without hard restriction.
  • Custom Warnings: Specify a clear reason message (e.g. "Velocities > 50 m/s may cause physics tunneling").
  • Customizable Theming: Pick custom warning border and text colors via ColorHex.
  • Collection Support: Validates elements inside arrays or lists individually via ICollectionElementAttribute.

2. Quick Start

csharp
using UnityEngine;
using MaharajaStudio.MSUltimate.Runtime;

public class Projectile : MonoBehaviour
{
    [ClampWarning(10f, 100f, "High velocities may require continuous collision detection!", "#e67e22")]
    public float launchSpeed = 50f;
}

Core Framework/Core Validation/[CompareWith]

[CompareWith]

The Problem: When editing dependent stats (like current vs max ammo, minimum vs maximum boundaries), designers must mentally calculate the relationship between separate fields or run into inverted values where min exceeds max without noticing.

The Solution: Add [CompareWith] to any numeric field:

  • Instant Relational Feedback: Live badge visualizes relation instantly without writing custom editor GUI code.
  • Multiple Display Formats: Choose between mathematical symbols (Symbol), completion percentage (Percentage), or ratio breakdown (Ratio).
  • Custom Accent Styling: Match status badges to your component aesthetic via ColorHex.

Core Framework/Core Validation/[RequireInterface]

[RequireInterface]

Restricts an Object field to only accept components or assets that implement a specified C# interface type, rejecting non-conforming objects.

1. Overview & Value Proposition

What it does: Enforces interface type contracts on Unity Object fields (GameObjects, MonoBehaviours, ScriptableObjects). When an assigned object does not implement InterfaceType, it rejects the assignment or renders an explicit error callout.

The Problem: Unity's serializer cannot natively serialize interfaces (public IDamageable target; does not appear in the Inspector). Developers often compromise with generic UnityEngine.Object or GameObject fields, leaving them open to assigning components that fail to implement the required interface.

The Solution: Add [RequireInterface(typeof(IMyInterface))] to any Object or MonoBehaviour field:

  • Interface Contract Safety: Enforces interface adherence directly inside the Inspector GUI.
  • Drag-and-Drop Filtering: Automatically checks dragged objects and extracts the implementing component.
  • Custom Error Callout: Displays error feedback when invalid objects are assigned.
  • Eliminates Null Casts: Prevents runtime GetComponent<IInterface>() == null bugs.

Core Framework/Core Validation/[ValidateInput]

[ValidateInput]

Validates a field's value in real time using a custom C# callback method and displays informative, warning, or error messages when validation fails.

1. Overview & Value Proposition

What it does: Executes a custom validation callback method on the MonoBehaviour or ScriptableObject whenever a field is edited. If the method returns false, it renders a styled feedback message box beneath the field with customizable severity (Info, Warning, Error).

The Problem: Complex game logic often requires multi-variable validation checks that cannot be captured by simple numeric ranges or null checks—such as checking that a string is a valid regex, verifying that weapon damage is not negative, or ensuring an inventory count matches maximum slots.

The Solution: Add [ValidateInput] to any field:

  • Arbitrary C# Validation: Run any C# boolean method receiving the field value as a parameter or checking instance state.
  • Message Severity Levels: Choose between Info, Warning, or blocking Error callouts.
  • Styling Customization: Customize message colors, padding, background plates, and font sizes.
  • Collection Elements: Can validate each element in collections (ICollectionElementAttribute).

2. Quick Start

csharp
using UnityEngine;
using MaharajaStudio.MSUltimate.Runtime;

public class PlayerAccount : MonoBehaviour
{
    [ValidateInput(nameof(ValidatePlayerName), "Player name must be between 3 and 16 characters!")]
    public string playerName = "Hero";

    private bool ValidatePlayerName(string name)
    {
        return !string.IsNullOrEmpty(name) && name.Length >= 3 && name.Length <= 16;
    }
}

Core Framework/Core Validation/[Validation]

[Validation]

Base class and foundational contract for all data validation and integrity guard attributes in MSUltimate, assigning them to the Validation execution pipeline.

1. Overview & Value Proposition

What it does: Acts as the abstract base class and category assigner for the entire MSUltimate Validation pipeline. Attributes inheriting from ValidationAttribute are automatically classified under AttributeCategory.Validation, ensuring consistent execution ordering, defensive fallback handling, and centralized inspector error aggregation.

The Problem: Custom validation systems in standard Unity or third-party tools are often fragmented, with inconsistent drawer lifecycles, ad-hoc execution timing, and poor UI Toolkit element synchronization.

The Solution: Extend ValidationAttribute when authoring custom validation rules:

  • Central Pipeline Classification: Automatically categorizes attributes into AttributeCategory.Validation.
  • Consistent Ordering: Standardized execution flow across all validation rules (Order sorting).
  • Extensible Base: Serves as the foundation for [Required], [ValidateInput], [ClampWarning], [CompareWith], and custom domain rules.
  • UI Toolkit & IMGUI Parity: Handles both legacy and modern UI Toolkit lifecycle integration automatically.

using MaharajaStudio.MSUltimate.Runtime;

[AttributeUsage(AttributeTargets.Field, AllowMultiple = false, Inherited = true)]
public class PositiveOnlyAttribute : ValidationAttribute
{
    public string CustomMessage { get; set; } = "Value must be strictly positive!";

Core Framework/Callbacks & Events/[OnAfterSave]

[OnAfterSave]

Automatically executes a C# callback method immediately after a scene or asset is saved to disk.

1. Overview & Value Proposition

What it does: Triggers a method automatically right after you save an asset or scene (Ctrl+S).

The Problem: In standard Unity, running code after a scene or ScriptableObject is saved requires writing an AssetModificationProcessor or UnityEditor.SceneManagement listener script. This separates your logic from the MonoBehaviour itself, making simple tasks like updating build stamps, writing dirty data to JSON, or logging save confirmations messy.

The Solution: Add [OnAfterSave] above any method or field in your component:

  • Automatic Post-Save Trigger: Runs seamlessly whenever the developer saves the current scene or asset.
  • Self-Contained Logic: Keep all save-related cleanup code inside the relevant MonoBehaviour or ScriptableObject.
  • Cache Invalidation: Perfect for refreshing asset registries, syncing data with disk, or clearing dirty flags.
  • Zero Runtime Overhead: Stripped out of player builds; only active in the Unity Editor.

2. Quick Start

csharp
using UnityEngine;
using MaharajaStudio.MSUltimate.Runtime;

public class WorldSettings : MonoBehaviour
{
    public string lastSavedTimestamp;

    [OnAfterSave]
    private void OnSaved()
    {
        lastSavedTimestamp = System.DateTime.UtcNow.ToString("yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss");
        Debug.Log("World settings successfully saved!");
    }
}

Core Framework/Callbacks & Events/[OnBeforeSave]

[OnBeforeSave]

Automatically executes a C# callback method right before a scene or asset is serialized and saved to disk.

1. Overview & Value Proposition

What it does: Runs a method immediately before you save an asset or scene, letting you sanitize or prepare data.

The Problem: In standard Unity, if a developer forgets to calculate derived stats, format metadata, or strip temporary runtime test objects before saving, bad data gets committed to version control. Unity offers no simple MonoBehaviour hook right before serialization happens.

The Solution: Add [OnBeforeSave] above any method, field, or property in your component:

  • Pre-Save Sanitization: Clean up null items, recalculate hashes, and format data before it touches disk.
  • Enforce Invariants: Automatically validate that references and numeric ranges meet project standards before writing.
  • Strip Temporary Data: Remove scratch runtime arrays, test spawn caches, or preview meshes cleanly.
  • Zero Runtime Overhead: Only runs in the Editor; completely stripped from standalone game builds.

using System.Collections.Generic;

public class QuestDatabase : MonoBehaviour

Core Framework/Callbacks & Events/[OnFieldBlur]

[OnFieldBlur]

Invokes a C# callback method when a serialized field or property loses UI focus (blurs) in the Inspector.

1. Overview & Value Proposition

What it does: Runs a method as soon as you click away or finish editing a specific field in the Inspector.

The Problem: In standard Unity, OnValidate() fires on every single keystroke. When typing a URL, math formula, or long dialogue line, firing validation on every letter keystroke causes console errors, frame hiccups, and premature checks while the developer is still typing.

The Solution: Add [OnFieldBlur] next to any serialized field or method:

  • Fires Only When Finished: Waits until the developer finishes typing and clicks or tabs away.
  • Batched Processing: Ideal for compiling heavy math, parsing JSON, or validating web links only once after input is complete.
  • Clean Field Verification: Verify capitalization, trim whitespace, or calculate hashes without interrupting typing.
  • UI Toolkit Native: Integrates directly with UI Toolkit's native BlurEvent lifecycle.

2. Quick Start

    }
}

[OnInspectorDispose]

Automatically executes a C# cleanup method when the object's custom Inspector is closed, deselected, or disposed.

The Problem: In standard Unity, if your editor workflow generates temporary preview textures, native memory arrays, async polling tasks, or scene handle listeners, they keep leaking in the background when the user selects a different object unless you write custom Editor.OnDisable() script boilerplate.

The Solution: Add [OnInspectorDispose] above your cleanup method or field:

  • Clean Deselection Cleanup: Automatically triggers when the user clicks a different GameObject or closes the Inspector.
  • Prevent Memory Leaks: Dispose native collections, release RenderTexture previews, and cancel cancellation tokens safely.
  • Counterpart to [OnInspectorInit]: Pair initialization and teardown logic directly inside the MonoBehaviour.
  • Zero Runtime Overhead: Only exists inside the Editor; completely excluded from final player builds.

Core Framework/Callbacks & Events/[OnStateUpdate]

[OnStateUpdate]

Periodically executes a C# polling method while the Inspector window is visible and active.

1. Overview & Value Proposition

What it does: Runs a method on a regular timer (e.g. every 100ms) while you are viewing the object in the Inspector.

The Problem: In standard Unity, the Inspector only redraws when an input event happens or when you actively edit a property. If you want to poll runtime server health, refresh live telemetry stats, or animate editor preview elements, you have to write heavy custom EditorApplication.update loops that constantly chew CPU cycles.

The Solution: Add [OnStateUpdate] above your polling method:

  • Configurable Tick Rate: Choose your exact interval (e.g. 50ms, 100ms, 500ms) to preserve CPU performance.
  • Active-Only Execution: Only ticks when the object is actively selected and displayed in the Inspector.
  • Live Telemetry & Diagnostics: Continuously pull live metrics, network ping, or memory usage without manually clicking refresh.
  • Automatic Cleanup: Immediately halts polling when the Inspector is closed or deselected.

2. Quick Start

csharp
using UnityEngine;
using MaharajaStudio.MSUltimate.Runtime;

public class NetworkHealthMonitor : MonoBehaviour
{
    [ReadOnly]
    public float currentPingMs;

    [OnStateUpdate(250)]
    private void PollTelemetry()
    {
        currentPingMs = Random.Range(15f, 45f); // Example live metric
    }
}

Core Framework/Callbacks & Events/[OnUndoRedo]

[OnUndoRedo]

Automatically executes a C# callback method whenever an Undo or Redo operation modifies the target object.

1. Overview & Value Proposition

What it does: Triggers a method automatically whenever you press Ctrl+Z (Undo) or Ctrl+Y (Redo) in Unity.

The Problem: In standard Unity, undoing an edit changes serialized field data in the background without notifying custom caching algorithms, mesh generators, or child component linkers. This leaves your scene out of sync with your internal data structures until someone manually modifies another property.

The Solution: Add [OnUndoRedo] above your cache rebuild method:

  • Instant Desync Prevention: Immediately recomputes matrices, procedurally generated meshes, or linked references after an undo.
  • Bi-Directional Safety: Handles both Undo (Ctrl+Z) and Redo (Ctrl+Y) operations automatically.
  • Zero Static Listeners: No need to manually subscribe to Undo.undoRedoPerformed.
  • Editor-Only Execution: Completely excluded from player game builds.

2. Quick Start

csharp
using UnityEngine;
using MaharajaStudio.MSUltimate.Runtime;

public class ProceduralPillar : MonoBehaviour
{
    public float pillarHeight = 3.5f;

    [OnUndoRedo]
    private void OnUndoRedoPerformed()
    {
        Debug.Log($"Undo/Redo detected. Recalculating pillar mesh for height: {pillarHeight}");
    }
}

6. Production-Grade Example

csharp
using UnityEngine;
using MaharajaStudio.MSUltimate.Runtime;

[ExecuteAlways]
public class GridSnapAligner : MonoBehaviour
{
    [Header("Grid Alignment")]
    [OnValueChanged(nameof(RecalculateSnap))]
    public float snapSize = 1.0f;

    public Vector3 snappedCoordinate;

    [OnUndoRedo]
    private void RecalculateSnap()
    {
        Vector3 currentPos = transform.position;
        snappedCoordinate = new Vector3(
            Mathf.Round(currentPos.x / snapSize) * snapSize,
            Mathf.Round(currentPos.y / snapSize) * snapSize,
            Mathf.Round(currentPos.z / snapSize) * snapSize
        );
        Debug.Log($"[GridSnapAligner] Synchronized snapped position: {snappedCoordinate}");
    }
}

Core Framework/Callbacks & Events/[OnValueChanged]

[OnValueChanged]

Automatically executes a C# callback method whenever a serialized field's value is modified in the Inspector.

1. Overview & Value Proposition

What it does: Runs a method immediately whenever you change a field or slider in the Inspector.

The Problem: In standard Unity, reacting to field edits requires using OnValidate(). But OnValidate() executes globally for the entire component on every single domain reload, scene open, and property modification, making it hard to know which specific field changed without tedious before-and-after cache checks.

The Solution: Add [OnValueChanged] directly onto the target field:

  • Field-Specific Triggering: Executes strictly when this specific field is modified by the user.
  • Optional Parameter Passing: Your callback method can optionally accept the new value as an argument.
  • Immediate Visual Feedback: Update material colors, regenerate procedural meshes, or update child transforms in real time.
  • Clean Configuration Flags: Configure whether to fire on load (InvokeOnLoad) or on inspector rebuild (InvokeOnRebuild).

2. Quick Start

csharp
using UnityEngine;
using MaharajaStudio.MSUltimate.Runtime;

public class LightAdjuster : MonoBehaviour
{
    [OnValueChanged(nameof(UpdateLightColor))]
    public Color lightColor = Color.white;

    public Light targetLight;

    private void UpdateLightColor()
    {
        if (targetLight != null)
            targetLight.color = lightColor;
    }
}

using UnityEngine;
using MaharajaStudio.MSUltimate.Runtime;

[ExecuteAlways]
public class CharacterAuraConfig : MonoBehaviour
{
    [Header("Aura Configuration")]

    [Range(0f, 10f)]
    public float auraIntensity = 2.5f;

    [OnValueChanged(nameof(OnColorChanged))]
    public Color auraColor = Color.cyan;

    [SerializeField]
    private ParticleSystem auraParticles;

    private void OnIntensityChanged(float newIntensity)
    {
        if (auraParticles != null)
        {
            var main = auraParticles.main;
            main.startSpeed = newIntensity * 1.5f;
            Debug.Log($"[Aura] Intensity adjusted to {newIntensity}");
        }
    }

    private void OnColorChanged()
    {
        if (auraParticles != null)
        {
            var main = auraParticles.main;
            main.startColor = auraColor;
        }
    }
}

Core Framework/Decorators & Visuals/[AdvancedCurve]

[AdvancedCurve]

Renders an enhanced, high-precision AnimationCurve editor field with custom graph colors, coordinate bounds, and background styling.

1. Overview & Value Proposition

What it does: Transforms standard AnimationCurve fields into styled, color-coded curve editors with custom graph coordinate ranges.

The Problem: In standard Unity, all curve fields look identical: a tiny green curve on a grey background locked to a default (0 to 1) coordinate box. When designing recoil curves, damage falloff, or camera shake that need negative values or specific ranges (like -180° to 180°), Unity's default curve picker requires opening multiple popup windows and manual panning.

The Solution: Add [AdvancedCurve] above any AnimationCurve field:

  • Custom Coordinate Ranges: Lock graph bounds (e.g. X: 0 to 10s, Y: -50 to 50) directly from code.
  • Color-Coded Curves: Set curve stroke color via hex codes (e.g. orange for explosion falloff, cyan for shield recharge).
  • Custom Dimensions: Adjust graph height and padding to fit comfortably into your inspector layout.
  • Embedded Labeling: Customize label colors, widths, and styling for quick visual recognition.

2. Quick Start

using MaharajaStudio.MSUltimate.Runtime;

Core Framework/Decorators & Visuals/[Breadcrumb]

[Breadcrumb]

Renders a stylized navigation breadcrumb trail above a serialized field to clarify complex subsystem hierarchies.

1. Overview & Value Proposition

What it does: Draws a sleek navigation trail (e.g. Combat › Abilities › Ultimate) above a field so you know exactly where it belongs in your game architecture.

The Problem: In large MonoBehaviours with 40+ serialized fields, it's easy to lose track of which category or subsystem a specific setting belongs to while scrolling through a long Inspector. Plain headers can get buried, and nested tabs can obscure parent context.

The Solution: Add [Breadcrumb] above key configuration fields:

  • Instant Architectural Context: Clearly indicates the domain hierarchy (e.g. Player › Movement › Wall Run).
  • Custom Delimiters: Use arrows (›), slashes (/), or custom icons as segment separators.
  • Color Accent Control: Tint breadcrumb chips with custom brand or system theme colors.
  • Zero Runtime Overhead: Only drawn in the Unity Editor; completely stripped from player builds.

2. Quick Start

csharp
using UnityEngine;
using MaharajaStudio.MSUltimate.Runtime;

public class PlayerMovement : MonoBehaviour
{
    [Breadcrumb("Player", "Locomotion", "Air Dash")]
    public float dashForce = 12f;
}

Core Framework/Decorators & Visuals/[ContextMenuItem]

[ContextMenuItem]

Attaches custom right-click context menu actions directly to a serialized field for quick resets, calculations, or presets.

1. Overview & Value Proposition

What it does: Adds custom right-click options to a specific field in the Inspector (e.g. right-click to "Randomize Seed" or "Reset to Default").

The Problem: In standard Unity, adding custom contextual actions to a component puts them under the 3 dots menu at the very top of the component header. When an action is directly tied to a specific field (like generating a GUID or resetting an offset), scrolling up to the component header is clunky.

The Solution: Add [ContextMenuItem] directly above the target field:

  • Direct Right-Click Menus: Right-click the field label to open your custom action list.
  • Multiple Actions per Field: Stack multiple attributes to attach several actions to the same field.
  • Cleaner Inspectors: Keeps the Inspector uncluttered by hiding rare utility actions behind right-click menus instead of adding large buttons.
  • Full Undo Support: Changes made by invoked context methods integrate smoothly into Unity's Undo history.

2. Quick Start

csharp
using UnityEngine;
using MaharajaStudio.MSUltimate.Runtime;

public class PlayerProfile : MonoBehaviour
{
    [ContextMenuItem("Generate New Guid", nameof(GenerateGuid))]
    public string profileId = "DEFAULT_PROFILE";

    private void GenerateGuid()
    {
        profileId = System.Guid.NewGuid().ToString("N");
    }
}

6. Production-Grade Example

csharp
using System.Collections.Generic;
using UnityEngine;
using MaharajaStudio.MSUltimate.Runtime;

public class TransformPresetRig : MonoBehaviour
{
    [Header("Default Offsets")]
    [ContextMenuItem("Reset to Zero", nameof(ResetOffset))]
    [ContextMenuItem("Snap to Ground (Raycast)", nameof(SnapToGround))]
    public Vector3 spawnOffset = Vector3.up;

    [Header("Direct Collections Cascading")]
    [ContextMenuItem("Re-verify Waypoint", nameof(VerifyWaypoint))]
    public Vector3[] patrolWaypoints = new Vector3[] { Vector3.zero, new Vector3(10, 0, 0) };

    [ContextMenuItem("Refresh Endpoint", nameof(RefreshEndpoint))]
    public List<string> endpointUrls = new List<string> { "https://api.game.io/cluster1" };

    private void ResetOffset()
    {
        spawnOffset = Vector3.zero;
        Debug.Log("[PresetRig] Offset reset to zero.");
    }

    private void SnapToGround()
    {
        if (Physics.Raycast(transform.position, Vector3.down, out var hit, 50f))
        {
            spawnOffset = hit.point - transform.position;
            Debug.Log($"[PresetRig] Snapped offset to ground surface at {hit.point}.");
        }
    }

    private void VerifyWaypoint()
    {
        Debug.Log("[PresetRig] Waypoint verified!");
    }

    private void RefreshEndpoint()
    {
        Debug.Log("[PresetRig] Endpoint connection refreshed!");
    }
}

Core Framework/Decorators & Visuals/[DeltaTracker]

[DeltaTracker]

Displays live numeric diffs (+/- change) beside a field to show how much a value has drifted since the Inspector was opened.

1. Overview & Value Proposition

What it does: Shows an inline badge (e.g. +2.5 or -10) beside a number showing how much you changed it during your current editing session.

The Problem: When balancing game parameters (like weapon recoil, player speed, or jump gravity), designers tweak numbers repeatedly. After several tweaks, it's easy to forget what the starting value was or whether you increased or decreased the stat.

The Solution: Add [DeltaTracker] to any float or int field:

  • Instant Change Readout: Automatically displays the difference between the initial session value and the current value.
  • Color-Coded Feedback: Accents positive and negative deltas with custom badge colors.
  • Configurable Precision: Control decimal place rounding (decimals: 2).
  • Zero Performance Hit: Lightweight editor-only tracking with zero allocations on repaint.

2. Quick Start

csharp
using UnityEngine;
using MaharajaStudio.MSUltimate.Runtime;

public class PlayerBalancing : MonoBehaviour
{
    [DeltaTracker(colorHex: "#F39C12", decimals: 1)]
    public float sprintSpeed = 8.5f;
}

6. Production-Grade Example

csharp
using System;
using System.Collections.Generic;
using UnityEngine;
using MaharajaStudio.MSUltimate.Runtime;

namespace MaharajaStudio.MSUltimate.Example
{
    [AddComponentMenu("Maharaja Studio/MSUltimate/Samples/Decorators/Delta Tracker Example")]
    public class DeltaTrackerExample : ModularMonoBehaviour
    {
        // ─── 1. Standalone Numeric Delta Tracking ────────────────────────────────
        [BoxGroup("1. Standalone Numeric Delta Tracking", BackgroundColor = "#0F172A", BorderColor = "#2563EB", BorderRadius = 6, MarginBottom = 8)]
        [DeltaTracker("#EF4444", 1)]
        public float playerHealth = 100f;

        [DeltaTracker("#10B981", 0, true)]
        public int combatScore = 1250;

        // ─── 2. Inside Custom Class Showcase ─────────────────────────────────────
        [BoxGroup("2. Inside Custom Class Showcase", BackgroundColor = "#0F172A", BorderColor = "#6366F1", BorderRadius = 6, MarginBottom = 8)]
        public VehicleTelemetrySlot propulsionTelemetry = new VehicleTelemetrySlot();

        [Serializable]
        public class VehicleTelemetrySlot
        {
            [DeltaTracker("#38BDF8", 0, true)]
            public float engineRpm = 4500f;

            [DeltaTracker("#EF4444", 2)]
            public float manifoldPressureBar = 2.45f;
        }

        // ─── 3. Direct Collections Cascading Showcase ────────────────────────────
        [BoxGroup("3. Direct Collections Cascading Showcase", BackgroundColor = "#0F172A", BorderColor = "#10B981", BorderRadius = 6, MarginBottom = 8)]
        [InfoBox("[DeltaTracker] implements ICollectionElementAttribute to automatically attach inline delta badges (Δ) to each row in numeric arrays and lists.", InspectorMessageType.Info)]

        [DeltaTracker("#10B981", 1)]
        public List<float> sensorTemperatures = new List<float> { 42.5f, 68.2f, 95.1f, 110.4f };

        [DeltaTracker("#F59E0B", 2)]
        public float[] calibrationOffsets = new float[] { 0.12f, -0.45f, 1.20f };

        // ─── 4. Interactive Simulation Actions ───────────────────────────────────
        [BoxGroup("4. Interactive Simulation Actions", BackgroundColor = "#0F172A", BorderColor = "#EAB308", BorderRadius = 6)]
        [Button("Apply Damage (-15 HP)", BackgroundColor = "#DC2626", TextColor = "#FFFFFF")]
        public void TakeDamage()
        {
            playerHealth = Mathf.Max(0f, playerHealth - 15f);
        }
    }
}

Core Framework/Decorators & Visuals/[DetailedInfoBox]

[DetailedInfoBox]

Renders an informative banner card with a distinct icon, bold title, and descriptive body message.

1. Overview & Value Proposition

What it does: Adds an expandable tutorial or documentation card (with title, message, and icon) above a field to guide designers on how to use it.

The Problem: Unity's built-in [HelpBox] is plain, single-level, and cannot be collapsed. Long documentation notes permanently consume vertical screen space, pushing critical gameplay variables down the page.

The Solution: Add [DetailedInfoBox] above any member:

  • Collapsible Content: Keeps the Inspector compact while making deep documentation accessible with a single click.
  • Title & Message Split: Separate bold headline from detailed instructional text.
  • Message Severity Themes: Support Info, Warning, Error, and None styling with matching icons.
  • Dynamic Visibility: Conditionally show instructions only when specific settings or states are active (VisibleIf).

2. Quick Start

csharp
using UnityEngine;
using MaharajaStudio.MSUltimate.Runtime;

public class SpawnerGuide : MonoBehaviour
{
    [DetailedInfoBox("Wave Spawning Rules", "Ensure spawn points have valid NavMesh surfaces before enabling endless mode.", InspectorMessageType.Info)]

Core Framework/Decorators & Visuals/[EditCounter]

[EditCounter]

Tracks and displays the total number of times a field has been edited during the current Editor session or across project saves.

1. Overview & Value Proposition

What it does: Displays a small counter badge (e.g. ✏️ 14) next to a field showing how many times it was modified.

The Problem: During level design and balancing passes, team leads and technical artists want to know which game variables are being modified frequently and which ones remain untouched defaults. Unity provides zero per-property edit telemetry out of the box.

The Solution: Add [EditCounter] next to any property:

  • Automatic Modification Tally: Increments a clean visual counter whenever the field's value changes.
  • Session vs Persistent: Track modifications during the active Editor session or persist counts across domain reloads (persistent: true).
  • QA & Balancing Insight: Identify "hot" variables that are undergoing heavy tuning versus neglected stats.
  • Stylized Indicator Badge: Styled with custom color accents and tooltip stats.

using MaharajaStudio.MSUltimate.Runtime;

Core Framework/Decorators & Visuals/[FieldBookmark]

[FieldBookmark]

Pins and bookmarks key serialized fields for instant 1-click navigation in long component inspectors.

1. Overview & Value Proposition

What it does: Pins a star or bookmark tag to your most important settings so you can jump straight to them without scrolling through hundreds of lines.

The Problem: In massive monolithic game components (like character controllers, inventory managers, or level directors), you frequently need to adjust 2 or 3 specific variables (e.g. "Max Health", "Debug Invincible", or "Spawn Rate"). Hunting for those 3 settings among 60 other fields wastes time.

The Solution: Add [FieldBookmark] above your essential properties:

  • Quick Jump Navigation: Registers the field into the MSUltimate inspector bookmark bar.
  • Custom Bookmark Groups: Organize favorites into named categories (e.g. "⭐ Combat Core", "⚡ Live Tuning").
  • Visual Star Accent: Displays a clean gold star icon beside the field row.

Core Framework/Decorators & Visuals/[FieldCooldown]

[FieldCooldown]

Enforces a temporary cooldown lock on a field after its value is modified, displaying an animated countdown overlay.

1. Overview & Value Proposition

What it does: Overlays an animated cooldown timer gauge directly on a property to lock rapid edits and visualize ability recharge times in the Inspector.

The Problem: Entering raw floating-point numbers (like 3.75s) for ability cooldowns gives no sense of gameplay rhythm. In addition, rapid repetitive modifications to expensive serialized properties can trigger costly recalculations.

The Solution: Add [FieldCooldown] to numeric properties:

  • Simulate Cooldowns in Edit Mode: Prevents rapid repetitive edits to expensive settings with an animated cooldown lock.
  • Radial & Linear Visualizers: Displays an animated countdown overlay or progress bar fill.
  • Custom Color & Message: Style the cooldown gauge with custom hex accents and "Please wait..." status notes.
  • Accurate Real-Time Feedback: Fine-tune combat cooldowns without building or launching Play Mode.

Core Framework/Decorators & Visuals/[FieldTag]

[FieldTag]

Injects a colored badge chip directly beside a field label to mark category, network authority, or safety tier.

1. Overview & Value Proposition

What it does: Attaches a clean pill badge (like [Server], [Client], [WIP], or [Audio]) next to a field's name.

The Problem: In team environments, designers and engineers often wonder which properties are synchronized over the network, which are client-only, or which are experimental work-in-progress. Plain variable names or comments are easy to overlook.

The Solution: Add [FieldTag] to any property:

  • Instant Category Recognition: Tag variables with clear visual tags like Server, Client, Critical, or Deprecated.
  • Custom Color Palettes: Set background and text colors to match your studio's tag system (e.g. red for Server, blue for Client).
  • Stack Multiple Tags: Attach more than one tag to a single property (e.g. [Network] + [Server]).
  • Clean Alignment: Aligns neatly next to the property label without pushing inputs off-screen.

Core Framework/Decorators & Visuals/[FieldTimestamp]

[FieldTimestamp]

Displays the last modified timestamp beside a field to track when inspector values were edited.

1. Overview & Value Proposition

What it does: Shows an automatic timestamp badge (like 2m ago or 14:32:05) right next to a field whenever its value changes in the Inspector.

The Problem: During tuning sessions, game designers tweak dozens of numbers across prefabs. When testing builds, team members often ask: "Did anyone change the boss speed?", "When was this balance tweaked?", or "Are we still using default values from yesterday?" Unity provides zero edit timestamp tracking.

The Solution: Add [FieldTimestamp] to any field:

  • Instant Audit Trail: See immediately when a serialized variable was last modified right in the Inspector.
  • Relative or Absolute Display: Choose between friendly relative time (e.g. Just now, 5m ago, 2d ago) or exact calendar timestamps.
  • Custom Tint: Customize badge hex color to match your studio styling or indicate sensitive balance fields.
  • Zero Runtime Overhead: Timestamp tracking runs strictly within the Editor GUI layer with no performance impact during gameplay builds.

2. Quick Start

using UnityEngine;
using MaharajaStudio.MSUltimate.Runtime;

    public float baseDamage = 45f;

Core Framework/Decorators & Visuals/[FilePath]

[FilePath]

Renders a file path picker with browse dialog, drag-and-drop asset support, and quick ping in the Project window.

1. Overview & Value Proposition

What it does: Turns a plain string into an interactive file selector with a browse button, asset pinging, and drag-and-drop asset handling.

The Problem: In standard Unity, string fields meant to hold file paths require developers to manually copy and paste file paths or open Explorer. Mistyped file paths, missing extensions, and broken relative paths cause silent asset loading errors at runtime.

The Solution: Add [FilePath] to any string field:

  • Interactive File Dialog: Click browse to open the native OS file picker filtered to your desired file extensions (e.g. .json, .csv, .bytes).
  • Drag & Drop Support: Drag any project asset directly into the string field to auto-populate its path.
  • One-Click Asset Ping: Jump directly to the file in Unity's Project window or reveal it in OS Explorer.
  • Relative or Absolute: Automatically formats paths relative to the project Assets/ directory or stores full absolute filesystem paths for external tools.
  • Collection Support: Fully compatible with List<string> and string array elements.

Core Framework/Decorators & Visuals/[GUIColor]

[GUIColor]

Tints the background and interactive elements of a field, property, button, or entire class using a unified hex color.

1. Overview & Value Proposition

What it does: Colors the background and controls of inspector fields, action buttons, or whole components using clean hex color codes (like #FF4444 or #3498DB).

The Problem: Inspectors with dozens of numeric inputs and buttons look uniformly grey and monolithic. Critical danger buttons (like "Wipe Player Data" or "Drop Database") look identical to benign helper buttons, leading to accidental clicks and mistakes during live development.

The Solution: Add [GUIColor] to any field, method, or class:

  • Immediate Visual Hierarchy: Highlight critical parameters, network values, or health bars with distinct color highlights.
  • Color-Coded Buttons: Make destructive action buttons vibrant red, save buttons green, and debug toggles yellow.
  • Class-Level Tinting: Apply to a class to give the entire custom component inspector a distinctive theme accent.
  • Standard Hex Codes: Use standard 6 or 8 character hex strings (#RRGGBB or #RRGGBBAA) for pixel-perfect brand consistency.

What it does: Removes the standard text label prefix from a field or property so the editor control spans the entire width of the inspector.

  • Array & List Cleanliness: Hides repetitive Element 0, Element 1 labels in collections when paired with list element attributes.

Core Framework/Decorators & Visuals/[Indent]

[Indent]

Indents a field or property horizontally by a specified number of levels to express parent-child relationships and visual hierarchy.

1. Overview & Value Proposition

What it does: Shifts a field horizontally to the right by one or more indentation steps (defaulting to 15 pixels per level) to clearly show sub-settings.

The Problem: When toggling options (like "Enable Shadows" or "Use Custom Gravity"), dependent sub-parameters are drawn at the exact same horizontal level as the parent toggle. Without visual nesting, inspectors look flat and confusing, making it hard to see which controls belong to which toggle.

The Solution: Add [Indent] to child settings:

  • Instant Visual Hierarchy: Clearly signal that secondary properties depend on or belong to the setting directly above them.
  • Configurable Indentation Levels: Pass 1, 2, or 3 to create deeply nested option trees.
  • Custom Pixel Step: Adjust PixelsPerLevel (e.g. 20f) to fit your studio's inspector layout guidelines.
  • Pairs with Conditionals: Combine with [ShowIf] or [EnableIf] for clean, expandable option sub-menus.

2. Quick Start

    public float bloomIntensity = 1.2f;

Core Framework/Decorators & Visuals/[InfoBox]

[InfoBox]

Displays an informative HelpBox banner with icons, severity levels, conditional visibility, and custom card styling.

1. Overview & Value Proposition

What it does: Renders a prominent callout box (Info, Warning, Error, or custom colored card) directly above or below fields and buttons.

The Problem: Complex components often require critical warnings (e.g. "Do not set below 0" or "Requires NavMesh"). Tooltips only appear on hover, and code comments are invisible in the Inspector, so designers frequently configure components incorrectly without seeing crucial instructions.

The Solution: Add [InfoBox] to any field, property, or method:

  • Severity Icons: Built-in standard presets for Info, Warning, Error, or clean borderless notes (None).
  • Dynamic Conditional Display: Use VisibleIf to display warnings only when specific criteria or invalid values occur.
  • Card Customization: Fine-tune background color, text color, font style, border radius, and padding.
  • Multiple Callouts: Stack multiple info boxes on a single property to show multiple status indicators or instructions.

2. Quick Start

csharp
using UnityEngine;
using MaharajaStudio.MSUltimate.Runtime;

public class SpawnerConfig : MonoBehaviour
{
    [InfoBox("Spawn radius must be larger than 5 meters to prevent entity overlap.", InspectorMessageType.Warning)]
    public float spawnRadius = 8.0f;

    [InfoBox("NavMesh baking is required for this enemy AI to pathfind.", InspectorMessageType.Info)]
    public GameObject enemyPrefab;
}

[InlineEditor]

What it does: Embeds the complete inspector GUI of referenced assets or components directly inside the current object's inspector, eliminating the need to click away.

The Problem: In standard Unity, editing a referenced ScriptableObject (such as an item definition or weapon config) requires selecting the asset in the Project window or locking inspectors. Designers constantly lose their place jumping back and forth between prefabs and asset databases.

The Solution: Add [InlineEditor] to any object reference field:

  • Zero Inspector Switching: View and edit ScriptableObjects, Materials, and Components inline in place.
  • Collapsible Card Frame: Expand or collapse the embedded editor with an integrated foldout header.
  • Scrollable Height Control: Set MaxHeight with scrollbars for complex nested assets to prevent overly long inspectors.
  • Custom Header Styling: Personalize banner background colors, text colors, borders, and margins.

Explicitly opts out a MonoBehaviour or ScriptableObject class from receiving global default component attributes.

1. Overview & Value Proposition

What it does: [NoDefaultAttributes] is a class-level decorator that instructs the MSUltimate inspector pipeline to completely bypass all project-wide default component attributes (such as auto-injected [HideScript], [Searchable], or default theme headers) for the decorated class and its subclasses.

The Problem: In large projects, teams often configure global default attributes in Preferences > Maharaja Studio > Default Component Attributes to ensure a consistent, modern UI across all gameplay scripts without adding boilerplate attributes to hundreds of classes. However, certain specialized components—such as low-level network drivers, third-party engine wrappers, diagnostic benches, or raw debug tools—need to remain completely free of injected decorations and retain only their explicitly declared code layout.

The Solution: Add [NoDefaultAttributes] to the class declaration:

  • Instant Exemption: The component is immediately shielded from all globally injected default component attributes.
  • Explicit Authoring Preservation: Only attributes directly declared on the class or its fields in C# are rendered.
  • Subclass Inheritance: Inherited by default across child classes, allowing entire inheritance trees (e.g. low-level transport classes) to stay exempted.
  • Zero Runtime Overhead: Implemented as a lightweight metadata attribute with compile-time reflection caching and zero garbage generation.

2. Quick Start

csharp
using UnityEngine;
using MaharajaStudio.MSUltimate.Runtime;

[NoDefaultAttributes]
public class LowLevelNetworkTransport : MonoBehaviour
{
    public int listenPort = 7777;
    public int maxConnections = 64;
    public bool enableRawSockets = true;
}

csharp
using System;
using UnityEngine;
using MaharajaStudio.MSUltimate.Runtime;

[NoDefaultAttributes]
[AddComponentMenu("Game/Diagnostics/Dedicated Server Telemetry")]
public class DedicatedServerTelemetry : ModularMonoBehaviour
{
    [Title("Raw Telemetry Pipeline", "Exempt from project-wide default component attributes")]
    [InfoBox("This component is marked with [NoDefaultAttributes]. Even when global defaults (like auto-HideScript or default headers) are enabled project-wide, this inspector renders exactly as authored without automatic injections.", InspectorMessageType.Info)]

    [Header("Network Socket Configuration")]
    public string serverAddress = "127.0.0.1";
    public int serverPort = 8080;
    public bool useTcpNoDelay = true;

    [Header("Buffer Endpoints")]
    public string[] activeEndpoints = new string[]
    {
        "/api/v1/telemetry",
        "/api/v1/heartbeat",
        "/api/v1/metrics"
    };

    [Header("Payload Protocol (Nested Class Showcase)")]
    public PacketSchema packetSchema = new PacketSchema("BinaryProtobuf", 1024);

    [Serializable]
    public class PacketSchema
    {
        public string encodingName;
        public int maxPayloadBytes;

        public PacketSchema(string encoding, int maxBytes)
        {
            encodingName = encoding;
            maxPayloadBytes = maxBytes;
        }
    }

    [Title("Diagnostic Actions")]
    [Button("Verify Exemption Status", ButtonHeight = 30)]
    public void VerifyExemption()
    {
        Debug.Log($"<color=#38BDF8>[Telemetry]</color> Running standalone without global default attribute injection. Port: {serverPort}");
    }
}

Core Framework/Decorators & Visuals/[Note]

[Note]

Renders an expandable note callout attached to a field with optional in-place editing, icons, and card styling.

1. Overview & Value Proposition

What it does: Attaches a clean, non-intrusive textual note or collapsible info card directly beneath an inspector field, with optional inline editing.

The Problem: Standard HelpBoxes and InfoBoxes take up substantial vertical screen space even when closed. When designing complex systems, developers want subtle, toggleable notes or scratchpads where designers can read or update instructions without cluttering the main inspector layout.

The Solution: Add [Note] to any field or property:

  • Collapsible or Inline: Expandable note toggle button keeps inspectors compact and clutter-free.
  • In-Place Live Editing: Set AllowEdit = true so designers can edit note messages directly in the Inspector.
  • Custom Card Styling: Fully style borders, background tint, padding, typography, and button icons.
  • Zero Build Footprint: Stripped automatically in player builds with no runtime overhead.

Core Framework/Decorators & Visuals/[ProgressBar]

[ProgressBar]

Renders a numeric field as an interactive, styled visual progress bar with dynamic limits and threshold colors.

1. Overview & Value Proposition

What it does: Converts numbers into animated, colored fill bars with custom heights, percentage displays, dynamic limits, and click-drag editing.

The Problem: Sliders in standard Unity are plain, single-line track bars with no visual fill color, no threshold warnings (e.g. turning red below 20% health), and no support for dynamic max limits read from other properties.

The Solution: Add [ProgressBar] to any numeric field:

  • Interactive Click & Drag: Scrub values dynamically by dragging directly across the colored progress bar.
  • Dynamic Limits: Bind MaxValue and MinValue to properties or methods on the object (e.g. maxHealth).
  • Low / High Threshold Colors: Automatically change colors when ratios dip below or exceed thresholds (e.g. green → yellow → red).
  • Flexible Overlays: Overlay percentages (75%), raw values (150 / 200), or custom formatted labels.

2. Quick Start

csharp
using UnityEngine;
using MaharajaStudio.MSUltimate.Runtime;

public class HealthSystem : MonoBehaviour
{
    public float maxHealth = 100f;

    [ProgressBar(nameof(maxHealth), colorHex: "#2ecc71")]
    public float currentHealth = 85f;

    [ProgressBar(0, 100, colorHex: "#3498db")]
    public float experienceProgress = 42f;
}
