Core Framework/Decorators & Visuals/[PropertyOrder]

[PropertyOrder]

Explicitly sets the display order of a field, property, or method in the Inspector. Lower values appear first.

1. Overview & Value Proposition

What it does: Controls the vertical sequence of fields in the Inspector using integer order values, regardless of their declaration order in C# script files.

The Problem: In standard Unity, the Inspector strictly follows the top-to-bottom variable declaration order in code. When deriving from base classes or organizing code logically for architecture, base class fields or helper variables end up awkwardly scattered across the Inspector.

The Solution: Add [PropertyOrder] to any field, property, or method:

  • Precise Vertical Ordering: Sort elements by integer rank (e.g. -10 draws at the top, 100 draws at the bottom).
  • Cross-Hierarchy Organization: Interleave derived class properties cleanly among base class properties.
  • Button & Method Placement: Position action buttons directly next to the fields they manipulate.
  • Clean Default Handling: Unordered properties maintain default order 0.

2. Quick Start

csharp
using UnityEngine;
using MaharajaStudio.MSUltimate.Runtime;

public class OrderedEntity : MonoBehaviour
{
    [PropertyOrder(10)]
    public string entityName = "Goblin";

    [PropertyOrder(-5)]
    [Title("Primary Entity Header")]
    public int entityId = 101;
}

The Solution: Add [RichTextLabel] to any field:

  • Word-Level Highlighting: Colorize and style individual words independently.
  • Dynamic Formatting: Combine font size tags, bold, italics, and custom hex codes in a single label.

using System;

using MaharajaStudio.MSUltimate.Runtime;

namespace MaharajaStudio.MSUltimate.Example

    public class RichTextLabelExample : ModularMonoBehaviour

        [Header("Security Rules & Thresholds")]

        [Tooltip("Bold red tag highlighting a vital security toggle.")]
        public bool enforceFirewall = true;

        [RichTextLabel("<i>Server Latency Threshold</i> (<color=#22C55E>ms</color>)")]
        [Range(20f, 500f)]
        public float latencyWarningMs = 150f;

        [RichTextLabel("<size=13><b><color=#38BDF8>TLS Encryption Cipher</color></b></size>")]
        public string cipherSuite = "AES_256_GCM_SHA384";

        [RichTextLabel("<b><color=#F59E0B>⚠ Maintenance Mode Active</color></b>")]
        public bool isMaintenanceMode = false;

        [Title("Nested Class Showcase")]
        public ClusterNodeSlot primaryNode = new ClusterNodeSlot
        {
            nodeIdentifier = "US-EAST-ALPHA-01",
            listeningPort = 8443
        };

        [Header("Failover Nodes Collection")]
        public ClusterNodeSlot[] failoverNodes = new ClusterNodeSlot[]
        {
            new ClusterNodeSlot { nodeIdentifier = "EU-WEST-BRAVO-02", listeningPort = 8443 },
            new ClusterNodeSlot { nodeIdentifier = "AP-SOUTH-CHARLIE-03", listeningPort = 8443 }
        };

        [Serializable]
        public class ClusterNodeSlot
        {
            [RichTextLabel("<b><color=#818CF8>Node Identifier</color></b>")]
            public string nodeIdentifier;

            [RichTextLabel("<color=#34D399>Listening Port</color>")]
            public int listeningPort;
        }

        [Title("Interactive Simulation")]
        [Button("Simulate Cluster Handshake", BackgroundColor = "#2563EB", TextColor = "#FFFFFF")]
        private void SimulateHandshake()
        {
            string firewallStatus = enforceFirewall ? "<color=#22C55E>ACTIVE</color>" : "<color=#EF4444>DISABLED</color>";
            Debug.Log($"<color=#38BDF8>[RichTextLabelExample]</color> <b>Firewall:</b> {firewallStatus} | <b>Latency:</b> {latencyWarningMs}ms | <b>Primary Node:</b> {primaryNode.nodeIdentifier}:{primaryNode.listeningPort}");
        }
    }
}

[StatusLight]

Displays a sleek LED-style status indicator light next to a field based on booleans, numeric thresholds, or conditions.

1. Overview & Value Proposition

What it does: Renders a glowing LED light indicator (Green, Yellow, Red, or custom colors) next to a field to signal health, connectivity, or thresholds.

The Problem: Looking at an inspector filled with connection strings, ping latencies, or state enums requires reading and interpreting numbers. There is no quick "traffic light" visual check to see if a system is healthy, struggling, or disconnected at a glance.

The Solution: Add [StatusLight] to any field:

  • Instant Traffic Light Status: Circular LED glows green for normal, yellow for warning, and red for error.
  • Dynamic Threshold Logic: Automatically evaluates numeric fields (e.g. green > 70, yellow > 30, red < 30).

1. Overview & Value Proposition

What it does: Pins a clean measurement unit label (like kg, km/h, sec, or %) or icon badge directly on the right edge of any input field.

The Problem: Numbers without units force developers to guess what they represent. Is a speed variable measured in meters per second, kilometers per hour, or knots? Adding units into variable names (speedInMetersPerSecond) creates bloated code, while omitting them leads to physics and design bugs.

The Solution: Add [SuffixLabel] to any field:

  • Explicit Units of Measurement: Display clear units (sec, m/s, rad, dB, px) right on the field.
  • Badge & Pill Styling: Render as plain text or as a stylish pill badge with background colors and borders.
  • Icon Support: Display accompanying icons (like clock icons for durations or ruler icons for distances).
  • Collection Cascading: Automatically attaches suffix units to elements within lists, arrays, and tables.

2. Quick Start

csharp
using UnityEngine;
using MaharajaStudio.MSUltimate.Runtime;

public class VehiclePhysics : MonoBehaviour
{
    [SuffixLabel("km/h")]
    public float topSpeed = 220f;

    [SuffixLabel("sec", colorHex: "#f39c12")]
    public float zeroToHundredTime = 3.8f;
}

Displays a prominent section title with optional subtitle, typography styling, background colors, and underline separators.

1. Overview & Value Proposition

What it does: Renders a bold, stylish title banner with an optional subtitle directly above a field, property, or button to introduce major inspector sections.

The Problem: Unity's default [Header] attribute only provides small text with no subtitle support, no background cards, and no alignment options. Breaking complex components into clear, magazine-quality visual modules is impossible with built-in attributes alone.

The Solution: Add [Title] to any field, property, or method:

  • Two-Tier Headline: Supports primary Title and secondary descriptive Subtitle in a single attribute.
  • Visual Underline Separator: Optional dividing underline for clean section separation.
  • Card & Banner Modes: Customize background colors, borders, corner radius, and padding.

Core Framework/Decorators & Visuals/[ToolTip]

[ToolTip]

Displays an informative hover tooltip over the property label or button in the Inspector.

Package: MSUltimate Core Targets: Field | Property AllowMultiple: False Inherited: True Performance: Zero Runtime Cost (Editor Visual Only)

1. Overview & Value Proposition

What it does: Attaches helpful mouse hover description tooltips to fields, properties, and buttons so designers can read documentation on demand without cluttering the UI.

The Problem: Unity's built-in [Tooltip] attribute works only on serialized fields and cannot be attached to method buttons or properties. It also suffers from inconsistent rendering bugs across custom drawer wrappers, and duplicating tooltips unconditionally across every list row creates immense visual fatigue.

The Solution: Add [ToolTip] to any member:

  • Broad Target Support: Works reliably on fields, properties, and method buttons.
  • Clean Inspector Interface: Keeps the inspector layout clean by showing detailed instructions only when hovered.
  • Opt-In Collection Cascading: Stay at the collection container level by default, or opt-in to per-element tooltips via ApplyToElements = true.
  • Zero Build Cost: Pure editor-time metadata with zero performance overhead at runtime.

2. Quick Start

using UnityEngine;
using MaharajaStudio.MSUltimate.Runtime;

public class TurretAim : MonoBehaviour
{
    [ToolTip("Speed in degrees per second at which the turret barrel tracks targets.")]
    public float rotationSpeed = 90f;

    [ToolTip("Maximum distance in meters before target acquisition fails.")]
    public float targetLockRange = 120f;
}

csharp
using System;
using UnityEngine;
using MaharajaStudio.MSUltimate.Runtime;
using Header = MaharajaStudio.MSUltimate.Runtime.HeaderAttribute;
using ToolTip = MaharajaStudio.MSUltimate.Runtime.ToolTipAttribute;

namespace MaharajaStudio.MSUltimate.Example
{
    public class ToolTipExample : ModularMonoBehaviour
    {
        [Title("Combat Defense Matrix", "Informative hover tooltips providing instant documentation for designers")]
        [InfoBox("Hover the mouse over any property label below to view contextual help and formula details without cluttering the UI.", InspectorMessageType.Info)]

        [Header("Vital Statistics")]
        [@ToolTip("Base vital hit points. When this drops to zero, the character enters an incapacitated state.")]
        [Range(100, 5000)]
        public int vitalHealthPoints = 1250;

        [@ToolTip("Flat damage reduction deducted directly from incoming physical and kinetic projectile strikes.")]
        [Range(0f, 150f)]
        public float armorRating = 45f;

        [@ToolTip("Percentage mitigation (0% - 75%) applied against fire, frost, and shock magic damage.")]
        [Range(0f, 75f)]
        public float elementalResistancePercent = 35f;

        [Title("Nested Class Showcase")]
        [@ToolTip("Demonstrates [ToolTip] applied inside child serializable shield models.")]
        public ShieldGeneratorSlot activeShield = new ShieldGeneratorSlot
        {
            shieldModel = "Aegis Kinetic Barrier Mk3",
            barrierCapacity = 450f,
            rechargeRate = 25f
        };

        [Header("Defense Perk Tags Collection")]
        [@ToolTip("Active defense perk modifier keyword slot. Cascades to elements via ApplyToElements = true.", ApplyToElements = true)]
        public string[] defensePerkTags = new string[]
        {
            "PERK_FORTIFIED_STANCE",
            "PERK_DEFLECTIVE_PLATING",
            "PERK_RESILIENT_WILL"
        };

        [Serializable]
        public class ShieldGeneratorSlot
        {
            [@ToolTip("Proprietary manufacturer model name for this energy shield.")]
            public string shieldModel;

            [@ToolTip("Maximum absorption energy pool before barrier fails.")]
            public float barrierCapacity;

            [@ToolTip("Shield points recovered per second after a 3-second delay.")]
            public float rechargeRate;
        }

        [Title("Interactive Simulation")]
        [Button("Print Combat Defense Readout", BackgroundColor = "#10B981", TextColor = "#FFFFFF")]
        private void PrintReadout()
        {
            Debug.Log($"<color=#10B981>[ToolTipExample]</color> <b>Health:</b> {vitalHealthPoints} | <b>Armor:</b> {armorRating} | <b>Resist:</b> {elementalResistancePercent}% | <b>Shield:</b> {activeShield.shieldModel} ({activeShield.barrierCapacity} HP)");
        }
    }
}

Core Framework/Scene & Gizmo Debug/[SceneArrow]

[SceneArrow]

Renders interactive directional 3D arrows in the Scene view to visualize heading vectors, velocities, and ray directions with draggable tip handles.

1. Overview & Value Proposition

What it does: Draws a 3D directional arrow directly in the Unity Scene view representing a Vector3 direction, velocity, or Transform orientation. Features live magnitude readouts, solid/dashed/double styling, and an optional draggable tip handle (Editable = true) to aim the vector directly inside the Scene view with live Undo.

The Problem: Tweaking directional vectors (like wind direction, projectile launch angles, or raycast offsets) by typing (x, y, z) values in the Inspector requires guessing angles and repeatedly testing play mode to verify direction.

The Solution: Add [SceneArrow] to any vector or transform field:

  • Instant 3D Visualization: See vectors immediately in world or local space in the Scene view.
  • Interactive Drag Handle: Enable Editable = true to click and drag the arrow tip directly in SceneView.
  • Length & Magnitude Display: Live distance/magnitude label displayed alongside the arrow shaft.
  • Inspector Visibility Toggle: Includes a 1-click eye button beside the field in the Inspector to show or hide the gizmo.

2. Quick Start

csharp
using UnityEngine;
using MaharajaStudio.MSUltimate.Runtime.SceneDebug;

public class TurretAim : MonoBehaviour
{
    [SceneArrow("#00FF88", Editable = true, ShowMagnitude = true)]
    public Vector3 fireDirection = Vector3.forward * 5f;
}

[SceneButton]

Renders interactive 3D clickable buttons floating in the Scene view to trigger methods or reset fields directly within the spatial viewport with live Undo support.

1. Overview & Value Proposition

What it does: Renders an interactive, clickable 3D button directly inside the Unity Scene view hovering above or offset from the GameObject. When clicked in the Scene view, it invokes the decorated method (or resets the decorated field/property) on the component with full Undo support.

The Problem: Testing runtime behaviors, spawning actors, cycling animation states, or executing calibration routines requires constantly shifting focus between looking at the Scene view and scrolling through deep Inspector panels to locate utility buttons.

The Solution: Add [SceneButton] directly onto any method, field, or property:

  • Spatial Clickable Action: Execute component methods directly in the 3D viewport without ever leaving the Scene camera.
  • Customizable Positioning: Position buttons in 3D space using OffsetX, OffsetY, OffsetZ or scale them with Size.
  • Theming & Color: Customize button appearance using hex color codes (ColorHex).
  • Inspector Toggle: Includes an eye visibility toggle beside the member in the Inspector to show or hide the 3D scene button.

[SceneGrid]

Renders a customizable reference coordinate grid in the Scene view on any cardinal plane (XZ, XY, YZ) for level editing, tile alignment, and spatial measurements.

1. Overview & Value Proposition

What it does: Renders an interactive reference ground or wall grid directly in the Scene view centered on the GameObject or origin. Supports custom cell sizes, grid dimensions, plane orientation (XZ, XY, YZ), axis highlight colors, and center anchoring.

The Problem: Placing props, aligning modular level pieces, configuring tilemaps, or verifying character spawn spacing against world measurements requires guessing distances or relying on Unity's global Scene grid, which is locked to world origin and cannot easily follow individual objects or orient along custom axes.

The Solution: Add [SceneGrid] to any transform, vector, or numeric field:

  • Object-Centric Grid: The grid moves and anchors directly to the decorated object's position.
  • Multi-Plane Alignment: Switch effortlessly between horizontal ground (XZ), 2D/vertical wall (XY), or side profile (YZ) planes.
  • Configurable Spacing: Set exact CellSize, GridWidth, and GridDepth to match level tiles or modular asset footprints.
  • Origin Axis Highlighting: Highlights primary center axes for rapid visual alignment.

Core Framework/Windowing/[ModularWindow]

[ModularWindow]

Configures window titles, icons, default dimensions, min/max limits, utility docking flags, and customizer toolbars for ModularEditorWindow and ModularMenuEditorWindow subclasses.

1. Overview & Value Proposition

What it does: Decorates custom EditorWindow subclasses that inherit from ModularEditorWindow or ModularMenuEditorWindow. Automatically configures tab headers, icon textures, default opening dimensions, min/max boundary constraints, floating utility behavior, and an integrated layout customizer toolbar button.

The Problem: Creating custom Unity editor windows normally requires boilerplate C# code to configure window minimum sizes, icons, title content, and dimensions, usually spread across static ShowWindow menu methods and OnEnable handlers.

The Solution: Add [ModularWindow] to any modular editor window class:

  • Declarative Window Setup: Specify titles, icons, and dimensions in a clean single attribute.
  • Enforced Min/Max Constraints: Guarantees windows cannot be resized below functional UI limits.
  • Utility Window Mode: Flag IsUtility = true for floating, always-on-top modal tools.
  • Built-in Customizer Hook: Toggle ShowCustomizerButton = true to inject the MSUltimate Layout Customizer directly into the window's toolbar.

2. Quick Start

csharp
using UnityEditor;
using MaharajaStudio.MSUltimate.Runtime.Windowing;

[ModularWindow("Quest Database", "d_CustomTool", width: 900f, height: 600f, ShowCustomizerButton = true)]
public class QuestDatabaseWindow : EditorWindow
{
    // Window content logic
}

The Problem: Editing complex nested ScriptableObjects or referenced components often requires pinging them in the Project window or losing your current Inspector context to view their details.

  • Side-by-Side Editing: Keep your main component open while tweaking referenced assets alongside it.
  • Custom Dimensions: Configure initial pop-out window width and height.
  • Custom Button Styling: Customize button label, tooltip, and hex highlight color.

Core Framework/Advanced/[Asset3DPreview]

[Asset3DPreview]

Renders an interactive, real-time 3D viewport directly in the Unity Inspector for 3D Meshes, Prefabs, Particle Systems, and Materials with orbit, zoom, pan, lighting, wireframe, animation controls, snapshot export, and collection showcase grid support.

1. Overview & Value Proposition

What it does: Adds an interactive 3D preview viewport right inside the Inspector, allowing you to preview, inspect, rotate, zoom, and test animations on models, prefabs, and materials without switching windows or dropping them into the scene hierarchy.

The Problem: In standard Unity, checking how a 3D model looks requires either dragging it into the active scene hierarchy, moving the scene camera around, or squinting at the tiny preview thumbnail at the bottom of the Project window. This breaks flow when tuning weapon drops, cosmetic skins, or modular environment props.

The Solution: Add [Asset3DPreview] above any GameObject, Mesh, Material, or collection of 3D assets. You instantly get an interactive 3D viewport:

  • Orbit, Zoom & Pan: Rotate with left-click drag, zoom with the scroll wheel, and pan with middle-click.
  • Lighting, Fog & Wireframe: Adjust key, fill, and ambient lighting, toggle wireframe view, configure distance fog, and toggle ground grid lines.
  • Turntable & Animation: Automatically rotate the model and scrub/playback animations directly in the Inspector.
  • Screenshot Capture: Capture high-resolution PNG snapshots (up to 4K, solid/scene/transparent backgrounds) with one click.
  • Collection Showcase Grid: When applied to List<GameObject> or Mesh[], renders an interactive multi-item 3D asset showcase grid.
  • Zero Runtime Cost: Editor-only execution stripped completely from player builds.

2. Quick Start

using UnityEngine;
using MaharajaStudio.MSUltimate.Runtime;

public class PropSpawner : MonoBehaviour
{
    [Asset3DPreview(PreviewHeight = 220f, AutoRotate = true)]
    public GameObject propPrefab;
}

7. Stacking & Compatibility Matrix

  • Grouping: Pairs seamlessly inside [BoxGroup], [TabGroup], and [CardGroup]. Set FullWidth = true when nested in wide cards.
  • Conditionals: Fully reactive with [ShowIf] and [HideIf]—the internal preview render texture and preview scene are disposed when the field is hidden.
  • Validation: Combine with [NotNull] or [Required] to highlight empty slots while displaying the interactive frame when assigned.
  • Defensive Fallback: If assigned an incompatible object (e.g. an Audio clip or TextAsset), safely displays a non-destructive fallback message without throwing GUI exceptions.
Core Framework/Advanced/[ColorPalette]

[ColorPalette]

Enhances Color and Color32 fields with clickable swatch presets from predefined project palettes ("Material", "Pastel", "GrayScale") or custom hex arrays.

1. Overview & Value Proposition

What it does: Attaches clickable color swatch buttons next to your Color fields, allowing artists and designers to pick approved project colors with a single click.

The Problem: In standard Unity, keeping colors consistent across UI, lighting, and materials is painful. Designers have to remember Hex codes, copy-paste color values between objects, or use the eyedropper tool over and over. A single wrong shade can make your game UI look inconsistent and unpolished.

The Solution: Add [ColorPalette] to any Color or Color32 field to display a curated swatch palette directly in the Inspector:

  • Predefined Palettes: Built-in support for "Material" (19 modern UI hues), "Pastel" (soft pastel tones), and "GrayScale" (monochrome values). If no palette or custom array is specified, automatically defaults to "Material".
  • 1-Click Selection: Click any swatch to immediately set the field's serialized color and apply changes.
  • Custom Swatch Arrays: Define bespoke brand or faction palettes using arrays of hex strings.
  • Custom Swatch Grids: Control swatch size, spacing, borders, hover highlights, and wrapping.
  • Dual Representation: The standard Unity color picker field remains optionally accessible alongside swatches.

2. Quick Start

csharp
using UnityEngine;
using MaharajaStudio.MSUltimate.Runtime;

public class UIThemeController : MonoBehaviour
{
    // Uses predefined "Pastel" palette
    [ColorPalette("Pastel")]
    public Color accentColor = Color.white;

    // Uses custom hex colors
    [ColorPalette(CustomColors = new string[] { "#FF5733", "#33FF57", "#3357FF", "#F1C40F" })]
    public Color primaryAccent = Color.yellow;
}

What it does: Creates a large, clear drag-and-drop landing box in the Inspector so you can easily drop single assets or bulk collections into your fields.

  • Visual Hover Feedback: The box lights up in green or blue when your mouse hovers over it with valid assets.

  • 1-Click Class Dropdown: Automatically finds all subclasses of your interface or base class and displays them in a clean dropdown.
  • Instant Creation: Pick a class from the list, and it immediately instantiates it and displays all of its fields.
  • Clear Visual Cards: Wraps the active class instance in a tidy, collapsible card with a header and border.
  • List & Array Support: Works seamlessly with collections, giving every item in your list its own type-switcher.

What it does: Makes private variables and C# { get; set; } properties visible in the Inspector without needing [SerializeField].

The Solution: Add [ShowInInspector] above any private variable or C# property:

  • Inspect Live C# Properties: View computed getter values in real time as your game runs.
  • Zero Serialization Overhead: Keeps your code architecture clean without forcing you to make variables public or serialize data you don't want saved.
  • Live Auto-Refresh: Updates periodically (configurable UpdateInterval) so you can monitor values during gameplay without writing GUI code.
  • Optional Read-Only Mode: Mark properties as read-only to prevent accidental edits while testing.

csharp
using UnityEngine;
using MaharajaStudio.MSUltimate.Runtime;

public class VehiclePhysicsController : MonoBehaviour
{
    private Rigidbody rb;

    private void Awake() => rb = GetComponent<Rigidbody>();

    [BoxGroup("Live Telemetry", Box = true)]
    [ShowInInspector(
        Label = "Current Speed (km/h)",
        IsReadOnly = true,
        ValueColor = "#00FFCC",
        UpdateInterval = 100
    )]
    public float SpeedKmh => rb != null ? rb.linearVelocity.magnitude * 3.6f : 0f;

    [BoxGroup("Live Telemetry")]
    [ShowInInspector(IsReadOnly = true)]
    public bool IsGrounded { get; private set; }
}

Core Framework/Advanced/[VisualDataChart]

[VisualDataChart]

Renders high-performance interactive visual charts (Bar, Line, Area, Sparkline, Stepped) directly above numeric arrays and lists.

1. Overview & Value Proposition

What it does: Renders beautiful Bar, Line, Area, and Sparkline graphs directly above your number arrays and lists.

The Problem: Balancing numerical progression curves—like weapon recoil over 10 shots, player XP across 20 levels, or damage falloff over distance—is really difficult when looking at a long vertical list of float values. You can't see the curve shape or spot sudden spikes without mentally graphing the numbers.

The Solution: Add [VisualDataChart] above any array or list of numbers:

  • Instant Visual Graph: Immediately visualizes your numbers as an Area, Line, Bar, Sparkline, or Stepped chart.
  • Multiple Chart Styles: Choose the right visual style for your data (e.g. Area charts for XP curves, Bar charts for audio spectrums).
  • Min/Max Guides: Shows clear scale markers so you always know the data bounds.
  • Real-Time Updates: As you edit numbers in the list, the chart geometry redraws smoothly in real time.

2. Quick Start

csharp
using UnityEngine;
using MaharajaStudio.MSUltimate.Runtime;

public class LevelProgression : MonoBehaviour
{
    [VisualDataChart(ChartType.Area, 75f, "#2ECC71")]
    public float[] experiencePerLevel = new float[] { 100, 250, 500, 900, 1500, 2400 };
}

Core Framework/Core Base & Infrastructure/[Decorator]

[Decorator]

Foundational base class for visual decorator attributes (headers, notes, badges, dividers) that augment Inspector presentation without altering serialized field values.

1. Overview & Value Proposition

What it does: Serves as the abstract base class and category assigner for all decorator attributes in the MSUltimate ecosystem. Attributes inheriting from DecoratorAttribute are automatically classified under AttributeCategory.PreDecorator, ensuring they are evaluated and rendered prior to the primary field drawer.

The Problem: Standard Unity DecoratorDrawer implementations are rigid, suffer from IMGUI spacing bugs, cannot easily bind to UI Toolkit visual trees, and frequently break layout stacking when multiple decorators are applied to a single field.

The Solution: Extend DecoratorAttribute when building custom decorative inspector elements:

  • Pre-Drawer Pipeline: Automatically positions decorations above or around the target field.
  • Pure Visual Augmentation: Decorators do not alter or hijack the underlying field's data serialization or interactive controls.
  • Robust Stacking: Seamlessly stacks with multiple decorators, notes, headers, and primary field drawers.
  • Foundation of MSUltimate: Powers core decorators like [Header], [Note], [Divider], and [InlineHelp].

2. Quick Start

csharp
using System;
using MaharajaStudio.MSUltimate.Runtime;

// Creating a custom decorative ribbon attribute
[AttributeUsage(AttributeTargets.Field | AttributeTargets.Property, AllowMultiple = true, Inherited = true)]
public class SectionRibbonAttribute : DecoratorAttribute
{
    public string RibbonTitle { get; }
    public string ColorHex { get; set; } = "#3498db";

    public SectionRibbonAttribute(string ribbonTitle)
    {
        RibbonTitle = ribbonTitle;
    }
}

Core Framework/Core Base & Infrastructure/[Drawer]

[Drawer]

Foundational base class for primary field drawers that control, replace, or customize how a field's interactive data is edited and rendered in the Inspector.

1. Overview & Value Proposition

What it does: Acts as the abstract base class and category assigner for primary field drawers across MSUltimate. Attributes inheriting from DrawerAttribute are categorized under AttributeCategory.PrimaryDrawer, establishing them as the primary rendering authority for the decorated field.

The Problem: Standard Unity PropertyDrawer implementations are difficult to chain, cannot easily communicate with decorators or validators on the same field, and struggle with custom collection element rendering.

The Solution: Extend DrawerAttribute when creating custom input controls or replacement fields:

  • Primary Drawer Authority: Replaces or restyles the main input control while maintaining pipeline interoperability.
  • Interoperable with Decorators & Modifiers: Works harmoniously alongside pre-decorators (headers) and post-modifiers (suffixes).
  • Foundation of MSUltimate Field Drawers: Serves as the base for attributes such as [MinMaxSlider], [Calendar], [DrawDateTime], [DrawRange], [DrawNullable], and [DrawTuple].

Core Framework/Core Base & Infrastructure/[FieldModifier]

[FieldModifier]

Foundational base class for attributes that modify field styling, labels, layout constraints, prefixes/suffixes, or interactive state without replacing the core drawer.

1. Overview & Value Proposition

What it does: Acts as the abstract base class and category assigner for field modifier attributes in MSUltimate. Attributes inheriting from FieldModifierAttribute are categorized under AttributeCategory.FieldModifier, allowing them to post-process, wrap, or modify an existing field's visual presentation (e.g. adding units, adjusting margins, locking editability) without replacing the underlying primary drawer.

The Problem: In standard Unity, tweaking simple presentation details like adding unit labels ("ms", "kg"), indenting fields, or locking a field to read-only requires writing custom property drawers from scratch or chaining cumbersome IMGUI calls.

The Solution: Extend FieldModifierAttribute when building field-level visual modifiers:

  • Modifier Pipeline Hook: Seamlessly attaches to the rendered field element to modify attributes, CSS classes, or inline badges.
  • Composable Stacking: Stacks cleanly with other modifiers, decorators, and primary drawers.
  • Foundation of MSUltimate Modifiers: Powers core attributes like [ReadOnly], [Prefix], [Suffix], [LabelWidth], and [Indent].

Core Framework/Core Base & Infrastructure/[Modular]

[Modular]

Foundational root base class for all MSUltimate attributes, establishing lifecycle execution phases, category classification, and order prioritization across the inspector pipeline.

1. Overview & Value Proposition

What it does: Acts as the ultimate architectural foundation for all MSUltimate attributes. Every attribute in the suite inherits from ModularAttribute, equipping it with an execution Category (PrimaryDrawer, PreDecorator, FieldModifier, PostDecorator, Validation, Behavioral, LayoutGroup) and an explicit sorting Order.

The Problem: Traditional Unity PropertyAttribute lacks execution phase awareness, making it impossible to predict whether a header renders before or after a slider, or whether validation checks occur before or after layout wrapping.

The Solution: All MSUltimate attributes extend ModularAttribute:

  • Deterministic Pipeline Execution: Categorizes each attribute into a distinct lifecycle phase.
  • Granular Sorting Priority: The Order integer allows fine-grained execution prioritization on members with multiple attributes.
  • Universal Stacking Contract: Guarantees decorators, validation rules, behavioral conditionals, and custom drawers compose seamlessly without conflicts.

2. Quick Start

csharp
using System;
using MaharajaStudio.MSUltimate.Runtime;

// Creating a custom behavioral attribute
[AttributeUsage(AttributeTargets.Field | AttributeTargets.Property, AllowMultiple = false, Inherited = true)]
public class LogAccessAttribute : ModularAttribute
{
    public override AttributeCategory Category => AttributeCategory.Behavioral;
    public string LogTag { get; set; } = "ACCESS";
}

Core Framework/Utilities/[MSIgnore]

[MSIgnore]

Opts out a field or property from MSUltimate's enhanced inspector pipeline, reverting it to standard native Unity drawing.

1. Overview & Value Proposition

What it does: Tells MSUltimate's inspector engine to bypass custom drawer processing, styling, and animations for the decorated field or property, forcing Unity to render the property using its default native editor GUI.

The Problem: In projects using third-party packages or complex legacy custom PropertyDrawers (e.g. specialized shader graph nodes, custom timeline tracks, or third-party serializable dictionaries), MSUltimate's enhanced UI Toolkit rendering pipeline might conflict with existing legacy IMGUI property drawer implementations.

The Solution: Add [MSIgnore] to any field or property:

  • Instant Fallback: Reverts the specific member to standard Unity rendering without modifying global settings.
  • Third-Party Compatibility: Ensures 100% interoperability with custom legacy property drawers from other Asset Store packages.
  • Granular Control: Apply only to problematic properties while letting the rest of your MonoBehaviour enjoy full MSUltimate styling.

2. Quick Start

csharp
using UnityEngine;
using MaharajaStudio.MSUltimate.Runtime;

public class LegacyInteropConfig : MonoBehaviour
{
    [BoxGroup("Enhanced Section")]
    public float movementSpeed = 10f;

    // Bypasses MSUltimate custom drawing and uses native Unity drawer
    [MSIgnore]
    public LayerMask legacyCustomLayerMask;
}
